+    tc.prices_entered_with_tax = True
+    tc.tax_calculation_strategy = TaxCalculationStrategy.FLAT_RATES
+    tc.country_exceptions.all().delete()
+    tc.save()
+
+    default_country = checkout.channel.default_country
+    default_country_rate = 21
+    shipping_address_country = "PL"
+    shipping_address_rate = 23
+    tax_class = TaxClass.objects.create(name="Product")

+            TaxClassCountryRate(
+                country=shipping_address_country, rate=shipping_address_rate

+        ]
+    )
+    for line in checkout.lines.all():
+        product = line.variant.product
+        product.tax_class = tax_class
+        product.save(update_fields=["tax_class"])
+
+    checkout.shipping_address = address
+    checkout.billing_address = address

Implement filtering by Collection references for attribute-based filters across pages, products, and product variants. Make consistent changes across GraphQL inputs, shared helpers, filters, and tests.

Scope and requirements:
1) GraphQL input support for collections
- File: saleor/graphql/attribute/shared_filters.py
  - In AssignedAttributeReferenceInput, add a new field `collection_slugs: ContainsFilterInput` with description: "Returns objects with a reference pointing to a collection identified by the given slug."
  - Update validate_attribute_value_reference_input to accept the new key "collection_slugs" as a valid reference filter key alongside page_slugs, product_slugs, product_variant_skus, category_slugs, and referenced_ids.

- File: saleor/graphql/schema.graphql
  - In input AssignedAttributeReferenceInput, add a new field `collectionSlugs: ContainsFilterInput` with the same description as above. Keep naming consistent with existing camelCase for GraphQL schema (collectionSlugs).

2) Shared helpers to fetch attribute values referencing Collections and to normalize global IDs
- File: saleor/graphql/attribute/shared_filters.py
  - Add typing import for cast since it will be used in new helper.
  - Implement collection helpers analogous to existing page/product/category/variant helpers:
    - get_attribute_values_by_referenced_collection_slugs(slugs: list[str], db_connection_name: str) -> QuerySet[AttributeValue]
    - get_attribute_values_by_referenced_collection_ids(ids: list[int], db_connection_name: str) -> QuerySet[AttributeValue]
    - Private helper _get_attribute_values_by_referenced_collection_identifiers(field_name: str, identifiers: list[str] | list[int], db_connection_name: str) -> QuerySet[AttributeValue]
      • Use product_models.Collection filtered by the provided identifiers (slug or id) and return AttributeValue filtered by Exists(collections.filter(id=OuterRef("reference_collection_id"))).
  - Add clean_up_referenced_global_ids(global_ids: list[str]) -> dict[str, set[int]]
    - Parse GraphQL global IDs (via graphene.Node.from_global_id) and group the numeric IDs into a dict of sets keyed by GraphQL type names: "Product", "ProductVariant", "Page", "Category", and "Collection". Return empty sets for missing types.
  - Extend _has_valid_reference_global_id to treat "Collection" as a valid type.

3) Extend page filtering to handle collections
- File: saleor/graphql/page/filters.py
  - Import the new helpers: clean_up_referenced_global_ids, get_attribute_values_by_referenced_collection_slugs, get_attribute_values_by_referenced_collection_ids.
  - Implement filter_by_contains_referenced_collection_slugs(attr_id, attr_value, db_connection_name) following the existing pattern used for categories/pages/products/variants:
    • If contains_all: return an AND aggregation of per-slug expressions.
    • If contains_any: return a single expression for all provided slugs.
  - Extend _filter_by_contains_all_referenced_object_ids and _filter_by_contains_any_referenced_object_ids to accept an additional parameter collection_ids: set[int], and incorporate expressions built from get_attribute_values_by_referenced_collection_ids for both "all" (AND) and "any" (OR) cases.
  - Update filter_by_contains_referenced_object_ids to:
    • Replace manual graphene.Node.from_global_id parsing with the new clean_up_referenced_global_ids helper.
    • Include the new collection_ids set when delegating to the _filter_by_* helpers.
  - Update filter_objects_by_reference_attributes to handle the new key "collection_slugs" by composing with filter_by_contains_referenced_collection_slugs.

4) Extend product filtering to handle collections
- File: saleor/graphql/product/filters/product_attributes.py
  - Import the new helpers: clean_up_referenced_global_ids, get_attribute_values_by_referenced_collection_slugs, get_attribute_values_by_referenced_collection_ids.
  - Implement filter_by_contains_referenced_collection_slugs(attr_id, attr_value, db_connection_name) similar to the pages and categories filters (both contains_all and contains_any support).
  - Extend _filter_by_contains_all_referenced_object_ids and _filter_by_contains_any_referenced_object_ids to accept collection_ids and merge expressions created from get_attribute_values_by_referenced_collection_ids accordingly.
  - Update filter_by_contains_referenced_object_ids to use clean_up_referenced_global_ids rather than inline graphene parsing; include collection_ids when calling the _filter_by_* helpers.
  - Update filter_objects_by_reference_attributes to recognize and process the new "collection_slugs" key.

5) Extend product variant filtering to handle collections
- File: saleor/graphql/product/filters/product_variant.py
  - Import the new helpers: clean_up_referenced_global_ids, get_attribute_values_by_referenced_collection_slugs, get_attribute_values_by_referenced_collection_ids.
  - Implement filter_by_contains_referenced_collection_slugs(attr_id, attr_value, db_connection_name) mirroring the product and page implementations.
  - Extend _filter_by_contains_all_referenced_object_ids and _filter_by_contains_any_referenced_object_ids with collection_ids, composing expressions using get_attribute_values_by_referenced_collection_ids.
  - Update filter_by_contains_referenced_object_ids to use clean_up_referenced_global_ids and include collection_ids.
  - Update filter_objects_by_reference_attributes to handle "collection_slugs".

6) Tests for collection reference filtering
- Add new tests to validate containsAny/containsAll for both collection slugs and referenced IDs, across pages, products, and variants. Follow existing patterns for similar tests on other entity types:
  - saleor/graphql/page/tests/queries/pages_with_where/test_with_where_references_collections.py
  - saleor/graphql/product/tests/queries/products_filtrations/test_over_references_collections.py
  - saleor/graphql/product/tests/queries/variants_where/test_over_references_collections.py
  Each test should:
    • Create reference-type attributes with entity_type=COLLECTION and assign AttributeValue instances that reference specific collections.
    • Assign those attribute values to pages/products/variants.
    • Query using where/filters with `reference.collectionSlugs.containsAny/containsAll` and `reference.referencedIds.containsAny/containsAll` and assert the result counts and identities per the scenarios.

Constraints and consistency:
- Keep naming conventions consistent: in Python inputs use snake_case keys (collection_slugs) and in SDL use camelCase (collectionSlugs).
- Reuse existing patterns for pages/products/categories/variants to ensure behavior parity.
- Ensure all queryset builders use .using(db_connection_name) and Exists/OuterRef patterns consistent with the existing code.
- Update imports as needed (e.g., remove direct graphene import where replaced by clean_up_referenced_global_ids).

evalCommits.spec:
Implement image/media validation and handling changes for the ProductBulkCreate mutation.

Required changes:

1) Update results construction
- File: saleor/graphql/product/bulk_mutations/product_bulk_create.py
- Function: get_results
- Behavior: Build results using a conditional expression per item instead of a list-level conditional so that each result is either:
  - ProductBulkResult(product=ChannelContext(node=instance, channel_slug=None), errors=errors) when instance is present, or
  - ProductBulkResult(product=None, errors=errors) when instance is None.
- Ensure the logic is functionally identical but expressed within each element (no if/else filter on the comprehension itself).

2) Validate media at input-cleaning time and pass GraphQL context
- File: saleor/graphql/product/bulk_mutations/product_bulk_create.py
- Method signature change: def clean_media(cls, info, media_inputs, product_index, index_error_map)
- Caller change: In clean_product_input, when media inputs are present, call cls.clean_media(info, media_inputs, product_index, index_error_map)
- Behavior for each media item (indexed by i) in media_inputs:
  - If neither image nor media_url provided: append ProductBulkCreateError with path=f"media.{i}", message="Image or external URL is required.", code=ProductBulkCreateErrorCode.REQUIRED.
  - If both provided: append ProductBulkCreateError with path=f"media.{i}", message="Either image or external URL is required.", code=ProductBulkCreateErrorCode.DUPLICATED_INPUT_ITEM.
  - If alt provided and longer than the limit (ALT_CHAR_LIMIT): append ProductBulkCreateError with path=f"media.{i}", code=ProductBulkCreateErrorCode.INVALID, with the existing over-the-limit message.
  - If image is provided (Upload mapping key):
    - Replace media_input["image"] with info.context.FILES.get(image)
    - Run clean_image_file(media_input, "image", ProductBulkCreateErrorCode). On ValidationError, call add_indexes_to_errors(product_index, exc, index_error_map, f"media.{i}") and skip adding this media item.
  - Else if media_url is provided and is_image_url(media_url):
    - Run validate_image_url(media_url, "media_url", ProductBulkCreateErrorCode.INVALID.value). On ValidationError, call add_indexes_to_errors(product_index, exc, index_error_map, f"media.{i}") and skip this media item.
    - If valid, compute filename = get_filename_from_url(media_url), fetch bytes with HTTPClient.send_request("GET", media_url, stream=True, timeout=30, allow_redirects=False), wrap as File(response.raw, filename), and set media_input["image"] to that File so downstream code treats it as an uploaded image.
  - Append the (possibly modified) media_input to media_to_create and return this list.

3) Simplify media persistence to avoid re-validation and network calls
- File: saleor/graphql/product/bulk_mutations/product_bulk_create.py
- Method: prepare_media
- Behavior changes:
  - For uploaded image (img_data := media_input.get("image")):
    - Do not read from info.context.FILES or call clean_image_file here. Assume clean_media already validated and transformed the data. Create ProductMedia with image=img_data (plus alt, product, type=IMAGE).
  - For media_url values:
    - Only handle non-image URLs (oEmbed). If not is_image_url(media_url), call get_oembed_data and create ProductMedia with external_url and oembed_data accordingly.
    - Remove the previous branch that validated and fetched image URLs here; images via URL are now converted to files in clean_media.

4) Keep error path formatting stable
- File: saleor/graphql/product/bulk_mutations/product_bulk_create.py
- Method: clean_variants
- Ensure the path field for variant errors uses a single conditional expression wrapped in parentheses: path=(f"variants.{index}.{error.path}" if error.path else f"variants.{index}"). Functionality remains the same.

5) Extend tests for media validation edge cases and add a test utility
- File: saleor/graphql/product/tests/mutations/test_product_bulk_create.py
- Imports: add from unittest.mock import Mock, patch; import PIL; import new helpers from saleor.product.tests.utils.
- Add tests:
  - test_product_bulk_create_with_media_invalid_extension: map an uploaded image without a file extension to a product’s media; expect no errors for the valid product, and for the invalid image expect code=INVALID, path="media.0.image", message="Lack of file extension.", count=0.
  - test_product_bulk_create_with_media_invalid_media_type: map a .jpg filename whose content-type is application/zip; expect code=INVALID, path="media.0.image", message="Invalid file type.", count=0.
  - test_product_bulk_create_with_media_image_with_invalid_exif: patch saleor.graphql.core.validators.file.Image.open so that getexif raises PIL.UnidentifiedImageError; expect code=INVALID, path="media.0.image", and the message starts with "Invalid file. The following error was raised during the attempt"; count=0.
  - test_product_bulk_create_with_media_with_media_url_invalid_image_type: patch saleor.graphql.core.validators.file.is_supported_image_mimetype to return False and patch HTTPClient to avoid real IO; pass a mediaUrl to an image; expect code=INVALID, path="media.0.mediaUrl", message="Invalid file type.", count=0.

- File: saleor/product/tests/utils.py
- Add helper function create_image_without_extension(image_name="product_img_without_extension") that returns a SimpleUploadedFile with JPEG content but no file extension in its name.
- Ensure existing create_zip_file_with_image_ext remains available and unchanged.

6) Wire changes together
- Ensure clean_product_input passes info to clean_media.
- Ensure imports remain correct at the top of product_bulk_create.py for HTTPClient, clean_image_file, is_image_url, validate_image_url, get_filename_from_url.
- Ensure behavior matches tests: errors from image validation map to the nested path under media index (e.g., "media.0.image" or "media.0.mediaUrl") and maintain exact messages produced by validators.file.

Acceptance criteria:
- All updated and new tests in saleor/graphql/product/tests/mutations/test_product_bulk_create.py pass.
- Uploaded images and image URLs are validated during input cleaning; prepare_media only persists objects.
- Invalid file extension, invalid mimetype, invalid EXIF, and invalid image type via URL yield ProductBulkCreateError with the expected code, path, and message.
- get_results returns entries for all inputs regardless of instance presence, using the new conditional expression formulation.
evalCommits.prompt: We need to improve media handling in the bulk product creation GraphQL mutation. Validate image uploads and image URLs during input cleaning, not during persistence. For each media entry, accept either an uploaded image or a media URL, validate it appropriately, and convert valid image URLs into file objects before saving. Ensure errors are attached to the correct media index and field, and keep alt length limits. Then simplify the media creation step to only create ProductMedia instances without revalidating or refetching. Also adjust the results construction to handle rows with and without instances uniformly. Add tests to cover invalid image extensions, wrong mimetypes (e.g., zip masquerading as jpg), invalid EXIF data, and invalid image types for image URLs, plus a small test helper for generating an image without a file extension. Keep the external (oEmbed) media flow for non-image URLs unchanged.

evalCommits.spec:
Implement filtering over attributes referencing Category across pages, products, and variants.

Scope and behavior:
- Support filtering items whose attributes reference Category objects by:
  - Category slugs via new reference input field categorySlugs
  - Category global IDs via referencedIds, with Category type accepted
- Semantics mirror existing page/product/variant reference filters:
  - containsAll: match only items referencing all specified categories
  - containsAny: match items referencing at least one specified category

Required changes:
1) saleor/graphql/attribute/shared_filters.py
- In AssignedAttributeReferenceInput, add a new field:
  - category_slugs: ContainsFilterInput
    Description: Returns objects with a reference pointing to a category identified by the given slug.
- Add helpers to fetch AttributeValue rows referencing categories:
  - get_attribute_values_by_referenced_category_slugs(slugs: list[str], db_connection_name: str) -> QuerySet[AttributeValue]
  - get_attribute_values_by_referenced_category_ids(ids: list[int], db_connection_name: str) -> QuerySet[AttributeValue]
  - Backed by a private _get_attribute_values_by_referenced_category_identifiers(field_name: str, identifiers: list[str|int], db_connection_name: str) using product_models.Category and Exists with OuterRef("reference_category_id").
- Extend _has_valid_reference_global_id to accept "Category" as a valid type for referencedIds.
- In validate_attribute_value_reference_input(), include "category_slugs" alongside existing keys in the allowed reference fields list.

2) saleor/graphql/page/filters.py
- Import the two new helper functions from shared_filters.
- Add filter_by_contains_referenced_category_slugs(attr_id, attr_value, db_connection_name) that:
  - For contains_all: AND a single-expression filter per slug
  - For contains_any: OR a single-expression filter over all provided slugs
  - Use _filter_contains_single_expression with referenced_attr_values resolved via the new helper(s).
- Update _filter_by_contains_all_referenced_object_ids(...) signature and implementation to include category_ids: set[int], AND-ing a single-expression per category ID using get_attribute_values_by_referenced_category_ids.
- Update _filter_by_contains_any_referenced_object_ids(...) to include category_ids, OR-ing a single-expression over get_attribute_values_by_referenced_category_ids for all IDs.
- Update filter_by_contains_referenced_object_ids(...):
  - Initialize and populate category_ids when the parsed global ID type is "Category".
  - Pass category_ids to the *_referenced_object_ids helpers for both contains_all and contains_any branches.
- Update filter_objects_by_reference_attributes(...):
  - Expand the attr_value type Literal to include "category_slugs" and "collection_slugs".
  - When attr_value contains "category_slugs", AND-in the result from filter_by_contains_referenced_category_slugs.

3) saleor/graphql/product/filters/product_attributes.py
- Import new category helper functions.
- Add filter_by_contains_referenced_category_slugs(attr_id, attr_value, db_connection_name) following the same pattern as page filters.
- Update _filter_by_contains_all_referenced_object_ids(...) to include category_ids handling (AND per id using get_attribute_values_by_referenced_category_ids).
- Update _filter_by_contains_any_referenced_object_ids(...) to include category_ids handling (OR across get_attribute_values_by_referenced_category_ids).
- Update filter_by_contains_referenced_object_ids(...) to parse Category IDs and pass category_ids to the above helpers.
- Update filter_objects_by_reference_attributes(...) to include "category_slugs" in the allowed Literal, and when present, AND-in the expression from filter_by_contains_referenced_category_slugs.

4) saleor/graphql/product/filters/product_variant.py
- Mirror the same changes as in product_attributes.py for variants:
  - Import helpers, add filter_by_contains_referenced_category_slugs.
  - Add category_ids handling to both *_referenced_object_ids helpers.
  - Parse Category in filter_by_contains_referenced_object_ids(...) and pass along category_ids.
  - Include "category_slugs" in the Literal and AND-in filter_by_contains_referenced_category_slugs when present.

5) saleor/graphql/schema.graphql
- In input AssignedAttributeReferenceInput, add the field:
  - categorySlugs: ContainsFilterInput
  - Include the description about referencing categories by slug.

Validation and tests (behavioral):
- Pages: where attributes reference categories by slug with containsAny returns two matching pages; containsAll returns one; by referencedIds with Category global IDs, containsAny returns three and containsAll returns two (according to sample fixtures).
- Products: both where and filter queries accept categorySlugs with containsAny/containsAll; referencedIds with Category global IDs behave similarly.
- Variants: where query accepts categorySlugs and referencedIds with containsAny/containsAll.

Notes:
- Ensure Category is recognized in global ID validation for referencedIds and properly decoded via graphene.Node.from_global_id.
- Ensure all new category filter pieces compose via the existing _filter_contains_single_expression helper used for other reference types.
- Preserve existing behavior for pages/products/variants referencing pages/products/variants.

Provide tests that cover slug-based and referencedIds-based filtering for containsAny and containsAll.

+def filter_by_contains_referenced_category_slugs(
+    attr_id: int | None,
+    attr_value: CONTAINS_TYPING,
+    db_connection_name: str,
+):
+    """Build an expression to filter pages based on their references to categories.
+
+    - If `contains_all` is provided, only pages that reference all of the
+    specified categories will match.
+    - If `contains_any` is provided, pages that reference at least one of
+    the specified categories will match.
+    """
+    contains_all = attr_value.get("contains_all")
+    contains_any = attr_value.get("contains_any")
+
+    if contains_all:
+        expression = Q()
+        for category_slug in contains_all:
+            referenced_attr_values = get_attribute_values_by_referenced_category_slugs(
+                slugs=[category_slug], db_connection_name=db_connection_name
+            )
+            expression &= _filter_contains_single_expression(
+                attr_id=attr_id,
+                db_connection_name=db_connection_name,
+                referenced_attr_values=referenced_attr_values,
+            )
+        return expression

evalCommits.spec:
Implement a refactor that extracts shared batching and attribute search vector logic into reusable utilities and updates all call sites accordingly.

Scope and required changes:

1) Add a core batching utility
- File to add: saleor/core/utils/batches.py
- Add function queryset_in_batches(queryset: QuerySet, batch_size: int) that:
  - Iterates a queryset in ascending pk order in batches of size batch_size.
  - Uses pk__gt start_pk to window slices; for each loop, fetch values_list("pk", flat=True) from queryset.filter(pk__gt=start_pk).order_by("pk")[:batch_size].
  - Yields lists of primary keys for each batch until no more results, updating start_pk to the last pk from the current batch.

2) Add attribute search utilities
- File to add: saleor/attribute/search.py
- Add function get_search_vectors_for_attribute_values(attribute, values, page_id_to_title_map=None, weight="B") -> list[NoValidationSearchVector]:
  - Build search vectors for assigned attribute values according to AttributeInputType with config="simple" and the given weight.
  - DROPDOWN and MULTISELECT: use value.name.
  - RICH_TEXT: use clean_editor_js(value.rich_text, to_string=True).

@@ -0,0 +1,17 @@
+from django.db.models import QuerySet
+
+
+def queryset_in_batches(queryset: QuerySet, batch_size: int):
+    """Slice a queryset into batches."""
+    start_pk = 0
+
+    while True:
+        qs = queryset.filter(pk__gt=start_pk).order_by("pk")[:batch_size]
+        pks = list(qs.values_list("pk", flat=True))
+
+        if not pks:
+            break
+
+        yield pks
+
+        start_pk = pks[-1]

evalCommits.prompt: Strengthen checkout line mutations against deadlocks and race conditions. Ensure that when adding or updating lines, the checkout is locked before any line operations, and that if the checkout disappears during processing, the mutations return a NOT_FOUND validation error on the id field with a standardized missing-node message. Introduce a shared constant for the missing-node error prefix and adopt it wherever missing node validation errors are constructed. Add tests simulating checkout deletion just before adding/updating lines to verify consistent error behavior, and adjust checkout-related benchmark tests to account for the additional locking query. Keep all other behavior unchanged.

evalCommits.spec:
Implement the following changes across the codebase to make checkout status updates gift-card-aware and to reliably trigger recalculations:

1) Recalculate checkout statuses using total minus gift card balance
- In saleor/checkout/actions.py, function transaction_amounts_for_checkout_updated_without_price_recalculation:
  - Import zero_money from saleor.core.taxes.
  - Before calling update_checkout_payment_statuses, compute checkout_total_gross as checkout.total.gross minus checkout.get_total_gift_cards_balance(). Clamp it to not go below zero using zero_money(currency).
  - Pass this adjusted checkout_total_gross to update_checkout_payment_statuses.

2) Update fetch_checkout_data to trigger status updates on price invalidation and to consider gift cards
- In saleor/checkout/calculations.py, function fetch_checkout_data:
  - Capture the previous value of checkout.price_expiration before calling _fetch_checkout_prices_if_expired.
  - After fetching/recalculating prices, recompute whether to update statuses based on either:
    - price_expiration changed compared to the captured value, or
    - force_status_update is True, or
    - current_total_gross is zero AND checkout has lines AND authorize_status is not FULL.
  - When updating statuses, compute checkout_total_gross as checkout.total.gross minus checkout.get_total_gift_cards_balance(database_connection_name). Clamp it to zero using zero_money(currency). Pass this to update_checkout_payment_statuses along with checkout_has_lines and checkout_transactions.
  - Ensure zero_money is imported.

3) Invalidate other checkouts when a gift card is used in an order
- In saleor/order/utils.py, function add_gift_cards_to_order:
  - After updating the gift cards’ balances and creating events, invalidate prices for any other Checkout records that are linked to the used gift cards (exclude the current checkout) by setting price_expiration=timezone.now(). Use a queryset like Checkout.objects.filter(gift_cards__in=gift_cards_to_update).exclude(token=current_checkout.token).update(price_expiration=timezone.now()).
  - Import Checkout in this module if needed.

4) Tests and test utilities adjustments
- saleor/checkout/tests/test_actions.py:
  - Add a parametrized test to assert transaction_amounts_for_checkout_updated_without_price_recalculation updates authorize/charge statuses correctly across multiple gift card balances with a transaction present.
- saleor/checkout/tests/test_calculations.py:
  - Add a parametrized test to assert fetch_checkout_data considers gift card balance when updating statuses with a transaction present.
  - Maintain the existing test for zero-amount checkout with lines and ensure it still updates statuses to FULL.
- GraphQL benchmark tests (saleor/graphql/checkout/tests/benchmark/test_checkout_mutations.py):
  - Increment expected query counts by +1 where applicable (as gift card/price recalculation adds one query) to preserve assertions.
- GraphQL mutations/tests (saleor/graphql/checkout/tests/mutations/test_checkout_complete_with_transactions.py):
  - In prepare_checkout_for_test test helper, force price recalculation by setting checkout.price_expiration = timezone.now() instead of pre-calling update_checkout_payment_statuses.
  - Fix redirectUrl typo if present and adjust stock setup where necessary for realistic availability conditions.
- E2E tests:
  - Add tests under saleor/tests/e2e/checkout/ to validate:
    a) Completing a checkout with partial transaction and gift card results in a completed order with zero total (no CHECKOUT_NOT_FULLY_PAID).
    b) Completing a checkout with only a gift card behaves correctly, including initial UNCONFIRMED status switching to UNFULFILLED after transaction commit hook; verify by re-querying the order.
    c) Completing a checkout that consumes a gift card invalidates other checkouts linked to that gift card, causing their statuses to drop to NONE and a subsequent completion attempt to return CHECKOUT_NOT_FULLY_PAID.
  - Ensure test GraphQL query for checkout includes authorizeStatus and chargeStatus fields for assertions.

5) Changelog
- Update CHANGELOG.md with a brief description of the bugfix: Checkout partially paid by Transactions and Gift Cards can be completed; statuses are recalculated using available gift card balance.

Behavioral outcomes:
- Whenever checkout statuses are recalculated (via actions or fetch), the required funds are computed as checkout total minus available gift cards balance, clamped to zero.
- Price invalidation (price_expiration change) reliably triggers a payment status refresh.
- Using a gift card on one checkout invalidates prices for any other checkout sharing that gift card, forcing their statuses to be recomputed on next access.
- GraphQL tests can assert authorizeStatus and chargeStatus, and e2e flows no longer raise CHECKOUT_NOT_FULLY_PAID when transactions plus gift cards fully cover the total.

Improve checkout payment status handling to correctly account for gift card balances and ensure reliable status recalculation:

- Update status computations so that the amount to cover is the checkout total minus the available gift card balance, never below zero. Apply this both when updating statuses after transaction changes and when fetching checkout data.
- Change the condition that decides when to refresh payment statuses during checkout data fetch to react to price invalidation rather than raw total differences, and still handle the zero-total-with-lines case.
- When a gift card is used during checkout completion, invalidate pricing for any other checkout that also has that gift card so their statuses update on next access.
- Extend tests to cover these scenarios, including e2e flows combining transactions and gift cards, and expose authorizeStatus and chargeStatus in the checkout query used by tests. Adjust expected query counts in benchmarks as needed and fix minor test setup issues.

Keep the solution consistent with existing models, helpers, and payment status logic. Don’t introduce new APIs; integrate with the current checkout payment status update utilities and gift card balance methods.

evalCommits.spec:
Implement concurrency-safe checkout price recalculation and update related tests.

Scope
- Core logic: saleor/checkout/calculations.py
- Fixture: saleor/checkout/tests/fixtures/checkout_with_prices.py
- Tests: 
  - saleor/checkout/tests/test_calculations.py
  - saleor/graphql/checkout/tests/benchmark/test_checkout_mutations.py
  - saleor/graphql/checkout/tests/mutations/test_checkout_lines_update.py
  - saleor/graphql/checkout/tests/test_checkout.py

Requirements
1) Concurrency-safe price persistence in _fetch_checkout_prices_if_expired
- After recomputing prices and setting price_expiration, do not blindly save recalculated totals/lines.
- Acquire a row lock for the target Checkout using checkout_qs_select_for_update() and filter by token, retrieving only last_change.
- Behavior when locked checkout not found (deleted or converted to order): skip persistence and return the recalculated checkout_info and lines objects as computed in-memory.
- When the locked checkout exists, compare the in-memory checkout.last_change to locked_checkout.last_change. Only if they are equal (no concurrent update occurred) persist:
  - Save Checkout with the specific update_fields used for totals, shipping, discount fields, currency, last_change, price_expiration, and tax_error.
  - Bulk update CheckoutLine fields (total_price_net_amount, total_price_gross_amount, tax_rate, undiscounted_unit_price_amount, prior_unit_price_amount) via checkout_lines_bulk_update.
- If last_change differs, skip saving and return the recalculated objects.
- Perform the above inside allow_writer() and transaction.atomic().
- Update imports in calculations.py to reference:
  - from . import CheckoutAuthorizeStatus, base_calculations
  - from .lock_objects import checkout_qs_select_for_update

2) Stabilize checkout_with_prices fixture
- In saleor/checkout/tests/fixtures/checkout_with_prices.py, when setting shipping method on checkout_with_items, also set checkout country from address_other_country and save both shipping_method and country fields in a single save (commit=False on set_country).

3) Add race-condition tests for recalculation
- In saleor/checkout/tests/test_calculations.py, add tests that:
  a) Delete checkout between tax calculation and save, using race_condition.RunAfter on saleor.checkout.calculations._calculate_and_add_tax to delete the row. Verify:
     - refresh_from_db raises DoesNotExist
     - the returned checkout_info/lines contain recalculated non-zero prices different from initial values.

evalCommits.spec:
Implement page reference attributes in product search and propagate updates via GraphQL mutations.

Scope
- Product search indexing
- GraphQL base mutation tracking (instance tracker)
- Page and PageType mutations affecting product search
- Save method signature unification across mutations

Requirements
1) Extend product search to include page reference attributes
- In saleor/product/search.py, when generating search vectors for attribute values:
  - If an attribute input type is REFERENCE or SINGLE_REFERENCE (page references only for now), include the referenced page title in the product's search_vector with weight B and config simple.
  - Introduce a helper that returns the searchable value for a reference AttributeValue (page title; empty string if not available).
- Ensure existing search update utilities continue to work without modification to their external API.

2) Add InstanceTracker support to Base GraphQL model mutations
- In saleor/graphql/core/mutations.py:
  - Extend DeprecatedModelMutation.__init_subclass_with_meta__ to accept a new Meta option: instance_tracker_fields (list of field names to track; default []). Store it on _meta.
  - In DeprecatedModelMutation.perform_mutation(): if instance_tracker_fields is non-empty, construct an InstanceTracker for the instance before cleaning/saving. Pass the tracker into save().
  - Update DeprecatedModelMutation.save() signature to accept an optional instance_tracker parameter and pass it through to overrides. The default implementation should still just save the instance.
  - Import InstanceTracker from saleor/core/utils/update_mutation_manager.py.

3) Update save() signatures in concrete mutations
- For all overriding save() methods changed in the diff, update their signatures to accept an optional instance_tracker parameter (default None) while preserving existing logic:
  - Account: account_address_create.py (AccountAddressCreate), account_update.py (AccountUpdate)
  - Staff: customer_create.py (CustomerCreate), customer_update.py (CustomerUpdate)
  - App: app_create.py (AppCreate), app_retry_install.py (AppRetryInstall; keep positional-only args while appending instance_tracker)
  - Checkout: checkout_create.py (CheckoutCreate)
  - Order: draft_order_create.py (DraftOrderCreate), order_line_update.py (OrderLineUpdate)
  - Page: page_create.py (PageCreate), page_update.py (PageUpdate), page_delete.py (PageDelete)
  - Product: product_create.py (ProductCreate), product_update.py (ProductUpdate), product_type_update.py (ProductTypeUpdate), product_variant_create.py (ProductVariantCreate)
  - Shipping: shipping/mutations/base.py (ShippingPriceMixin.save)
  - Tax: tax_class_create.py (TaxClassCreate), tax_class_update.py (TaxClassUpdate), tax_configuration_update.py (TaxConfigurationUpdate)
  - Webhook: webhook_create.py (WebhookCreate), webhook_update.py (WebhookUpdate)
- No behavioral changes are required in these methods except for handling the optional instance_tracker when needed (see #4).

4) Use InstanceTracker in PageUpdate to trigger product search updates
- In saleor/graphql/page/mutations/page_update.py:
  - Set Meta.instance_tracker_fields to ["title"].
  - In save(), after calling the parent save, if the instance_tracker reports that title changed, trigger an update routine to mark impacted products for search reindex.

5) Mark products referencing pages/page types as search-index dirty on delete/bulk delete and relevant updates
- Add a helper to lock Product rows deterministically:
  - saleor/product/lock_objects.py: implement product_qs_select_for_update() returning Product.objects ordered by pk with select_for_update(of=(['self'])).
- Page delete (saleor/graphql/page/mutations/page_delete.py):
  - Before performing the delete, mark products that reference the page via AssignedProductAttributeValue → AttributeValue(reference_page=page) as search_index_dirty=True.
  - Use transaction.atomic() and product_qs_select_for_update(); determine product IDs using EXISTS subqueries (no explicit JOIN). Then bulk update those products.
- Page type delete (saleor/graphql/page/mutations/page_type_delete.py):
  - Similarly, mark products referencing any pages under the page type as search_index_dirty=True. Compute page_ids for the page type, then products via EXISTS subqueries. Lock products and update within a transaction.
- Page bulk delete (saleor/graphql/page/bulk_mutations.py):
  - For the set of pages being deleted, mark products referencing them as search_index_dirty=True using the same pattern (EXISTS + locking + transaction) before performing bulk deletion.
- Page type bulk delete (saleor/graphql/page/bulk_mutations.py):
  - For the set of page types being deleted, compute page_ids across those types and mark products referencing them as search_index_dirty=True with the same pattern.
- Keep existing behavior of removing AssignedPageAttributeValue and invoking events; only add the product search dirtying step.

6) Use EXISTS subqueries and transactions
- Replace joins with EXISTS subqueries when identifying impacted products that have AttributeValue.reference_page pointing to the targeted pages. Wrap updates in transaction.atomic() and lock product rows using product_qs_select_for_update() before updating search_index_dirty.

7) Import adjustments
- When adding EXISTS-based logic in page bulk mutations, import Exists and OuterRef from django.db.models rather than django.db.models.expressions.
- Import product_qs_select_for_update and Product where needed in page mutations.

Behavioral outcome
- Product search vectors include text from referenced pages (page title) via page reference attributes.
- When a page title changes, related products are marked dirty and reindexing removes old page titles and includes the updated one.
- When a page or page type is deleted (including bulk operations), related products are marked dirty so subsequent reindexing removes the deleted page’s title from their search vectors.
- GraphQL mutation save() methods accept an optional instance_tracker; the base mutation creates and passes it when instance_tracker_fields are configured.

Add support for indexing referenced page information in product search and ensure product search stays consistent when related pages are modified or removed.

Specifically:
- Extend product search so that products include the titles of referenced pages (via reference attributes) in their search index.
- Introduce an instance change tracking mechanism in the base GraphQL model mutation so individual mutations can react to field changes; expose a way for mutations to declare fields to track and receive a tracker in their save.
- Update page-related mutations so that when pages or page types are updated or deleted (individually or in bulk), any products that reference them are marked for search reindexing. Use efficient EXISTS-based queries and lock products while updating.
- Update mutation save methods across the code to accept an optional instance tracker parameter, preserving existing behavior.

Ensure you cover both single and bulk delete flows for pages and page types, and trigger reindexing when a page title changes. Use transactions and row locking where appropriate to avoid race conditions.

Implement a refactor that relocates page-attribute filtering logic from the shared attribute module into the page module and updates imports accordingly.

Make the following changes:

1) In saleor/graphql/attribute/shared_filters.py
- Remove high-level filtering functions that build Q expressions for both pages and products. Specifically delete:
  - filter_objects_by_attributes
  - filter_objects_by_reference_attributes
  - filter_by_contains_referenced_object_ids
  - _filter_contains_single_expression
  - _filter_contains_all_condition
  - _filter_contains_any_condition
  - filter_by_contains_referenced_pages
  - filter_by_contains_referenced_products
  - filter_by_contains_referenced_variants
  - filter_by_slug_or_name
  - filter_by_numeric_attribute
  - filter_by_boolean_attribute
  - filter_by_date_attribute
  - filter_by_date_time_attribute
- Retain and continue exporting only:
  - GraphQL input classes for attribute where input
  - Validation functions (validate_attribute_value_input, validate_attribute_value_reference_input)
  - AttributeValue getter utilities (get_attribute_values_by_*), including for slug/name, numeric, boolean, date, date_time, and referenced pages/products/variants (by ids/slugs/skus)
- Update imports to remove unused Q (keep Exists, OuterRef, QuerySet).

2) In saleor/graphql/page/filters.py
- Replace the previous delegation to shared filter_objects_by_attributes with a page-specific implementation and add the necessary helpers:
  - Add _get_assigned_page_attribute_for_attribute_value(attribute_values, db_connection_name) that returns a Q(Exists(...)) over AssignedPageAttributeValue with a value_id subquery.
  - Implement page-local filter helpers that return Q expressions by leveraging the shared AttributeValue getter utilities:
    - filter_by_slug_or_name(attr_id, attr_value, db_connection_name)
    - filter_by_numeric_attribute(attr_id, numeric_value, db_connection_name)
    - filter_by_boolean_attribute(attr_id, boolean_value, db_connection_name)
    - filter_by_date_attribute(attr_id, date_value, db_connection_name)
    - filter_by_date_time_attribute(attr_id, date_value, db_connection_name)
  - Implement reference attribute helpers for pages:
    - _filter_contains_single_expression(attr_id, db_connection_name, referenced_attr_values) that optionally filters by attribute_id and wraps with _get_assigned_page_attribute_for_attribute_value
    - filter_by_contains_referenced_page_slugs(attr_id, attr_value, db_connection_name)
    - filter_by_contains_referenced_product_slugs(attr_id, attr_value, db_connection_name)
    - filter_by_contains_referenced_variant_skus(attr_id, attr_value, db_connection_name)
    - _filter_by_contains_all_referenced_object_ids(...) and _filter_by_contains_any_referenced_object_ids(...) that combine page/product/variant references using AND/OR semantics
    - filter_by_contains_referenced_object_ids(attr_id, attr_value, db_connection_name) that parses GraphQL global IDs (Page/Product/ProductVariant) via graphene.Node.from_global_id and delegates to the helper above
    - filter_objects_by_reference_attributes(attr_id, attr_value, db_connection_name) that composes referenced_ids, page_slugs, product_slugs, and product_variant_skus filters
  - Re-implement filter_pages_by_attributes(qs, value) locally for pages, mirroring the prior generic flow:
    - Resolve attribute slugs to Attribute rows, short-circuit to qs.none() for any unknown slug
    - If a filter has a slug without a value, produce a Q expression matching any assigned value for that attribute via AssignedPageAttributeValue
    - For filters with value, branch by the provided value key (slug, name, numeric, boolean, date, date_time, reference) and compose Q expressions using the page-local helpers
    - If any composed expression exists, return qs.filter(expression), else qs.none()
- Update imports in this file to include:
  - typing.Literal
  - django.db.models: Exists, OuterRef, Q, QuerySet
  - Attribute and AttributeValue models
  - From ..attribute.shared_filters: AssignedAttributeWhereInput, CONTAINS_TYPING, all get_attribute_values_by_* helpers, and validate_attribute_value_input
  - From ..utils.filters: Number and existing filter helpers
- Keep PageWhere.is_valid calling validate_attribute_value_input unchanged.

3) Ensure no remaining references to the deleted shared functions exist in page filters. Product filters keep their own local versions and do not import the removed shared functions, so no changes are required outside the two edited files.

4) Behavior and API expectations
- GraphQL where filtering for pages by attributes must continue to support:
  - slug/name string filters, numeric/boolean/date/date_time filters, and reference filters with contains_all/contains_any for referenced_ids (global IDs) or page_slugs/product_slugs/product_variant_skus
  - Mixed attribute inputs across multiple attributes combining with logical AND
  - Attributes provided without a value returning pages that have any value for that attribute
- Validation of attribute value input remains in shared_filters and is invoked in PageWhere.is_valid.

5) Lint/typing hygiene
- Because shared_filters.py no longer constructs Q expressions, remove the unused Q import and any other unused imports in that file.
- In page/filters.py add the new imports and ensure type hints: QuerySet[AttributeValue] where applicable, and Number for numeric filters.

+def filter_by_contains_referenced_page_slugs(
+    attr_id: int | None,

+):
+    """Build an expression to filter pages based on their references to pages.

+    specified pages will match.
+    - If `contains_any` is provided, pages that reference at least one of

+    contains_all = attr_value.get("contains_all")
+    contains_any = attr_value.get("contains_any")
+
+    if contains_all:
+        expression = Q()
+        for page_slug in contains_all:
+            referenced_attr_values = get_attribute_values_by_referenced_page_slugs(
+                slugs=[page_slug], db_connection_name=db_connection_name

+            expression &= _filter_contains_single_expression(

+

+    for obj_id in contains_any or contains_all or []:

+            product_ids=product_ids,

+    if contains_any:

+            variant_ids=variant_ids,
+            product_ids=product_ids,

+        ],

+

+            attr_id,
+            attr_value["referenced_ids"],

+        )
+    if "page_slugs" in attr_value:
+        filter_expression &= filter_by_contains_referenced_page_slugs(
+            attr_id,
+            attr_value["page_slugs"],
+            db_connection_name,
+        )
+    if "product_slugs" in attr_value:
+        filter_expression &= filter_by_contains_referenced_product_slugs(
+            attr_id,
+            attr_value["product_slugs"],
+            db_connection_name,
+        )
+    if "product_variant_skus" in attr_value:
+        filter_expression &= filter_by_contains_referenced_variant_skus(
+            attr_id,
+            attr_value["product_variant_skus"],
+            db_connection_name,
+        )
+    return filter_expression
+
+
+def filter_pages_by_attributes(qs, value):
+    attribute_slugs = {
+        attr_filter["slug"] for attr_filter in value if "slug" in attr_filter
+    }
+    attributes_map = {
+        attr.slug: attr
+        for attr in Attribute.objects.using(qs.db).filter(slug__in=attribute_slugs)
+    }
+    if len(attribute_slugs) != len(attributes_map.keys()):
+        # Filter over non existing attribute
+        return qs.none()
+
+    attr_filter_expression = Q()
+
+    attr_without_values_input = []
+    for attr_filter in value:
+        if "slug" in attr_filter and "value" not in attr_filter:
+            attr_without_values_input.append(attributes_map[attr_filter["slug"]])
+
+    if attr_without_values_input:
+        atr_value_qs = AttributeValue.objects.using(qs.db).filter(
+            attribute_id__in=[attr.id for attr in attr_without_values_input]
+        )
+        assigned_attr_value = AssignedPageAttributeValue.objects.using(qs.db).filter(
+            Exists(atr_value_qs.filter(id=OuterRef("value_id"))),
+            page_id=OuterRef("id"),
+        )
+        attr_filter_expression = Q(Exists(assigned_attr_value))
+
+    for attr_filter in value:
+        attr_value = attr_filter.get("value")
+        if not attr_value:
+            # attrs without value input are handled separately
+            continue
+
+        attr_id = None
+        if attr_slug := attr_filter.get("slug"):
+            attr = attributes_map[attr_slug]
+            attr_id = attr.id
+
+        attr_value = attr_filter["value"]
+
+        if "slug" in attr_value or "name" in attr_value:
+            attr_filter_expression &= filter_by_slug_or_name(
+                attr_id,
+                attr_value,
+                qs.db,
+            )
+        elif "numeric" in attr_value:
+            attr_filter_expression &= filter_by_numeric_attribute(
+                attr_id,
+                attr_value["numeric"],
+                qs.db,
+            )
+        elif "boolean" in attr_value:
+            attr_filter_expression &= filter_by_boolean_attribute(
+                attr_id,
+                attr_value["boolean"],
+                qs.db,
+            )
+        elif "date" in attr_value:
+            attr_filter_expression &= filter_by_date_attribute(
+                attr_id,
+                attr_value["date"],
+                qs.db,
+            )
+        elif "date_time" in attr_value:
+            attr_filter_expression &= filter_by_date_time_attribute(
+                attr_id,
+                attr_value["date_time"],
+                qs.db,
+            )
+        elif "reference" in attr_value:
+            attr_filter_expression &= filter_objects_by_reference_attributes(
+                attr_id,
+                attr_value["reference"],
+                qs.db,
+            )
+    if attr_filter_expression != Q():
+        return qs.filter(attr_filter_expression)
+    return qs.none()
+

evalCommits.spec:
Implement warehouse-based filtering for orders via fulfillment data.

Scope of changes:
1) GraphQL order filtering (Python):
- In saleor/graphql/order/filters.py:
  - Add necessary imports to support typing and model traversal for warehouses used in fulfillments (Mapping, QuerySet; FulfillmentLine, Stock, Warehouse).
  - Implement a helper that, given a fulfillment queryset and warehouse filter input, restricts fulfillments to those that have at least one line whose stock belongs to a warehouse matching the input. The input supports filtering by:
    - id (GlobalIDFilterInput)
    - slug (StringFilterInput)
    - external_reference (StringFilterInput)
    The helper must:
    - Return an empty queryset when no warehouse filter values are provided.
    - Combine id/slug/external_reference constraints on Warehouse appropriately.
    - Narrow Stocks by matching the Warehouse(s).
    - Narrow FulfillmentLines by matching the Stock(s).
    - Narrow fulfillments to those referenced by those FulfillmentLines.
    - Use the existing queryset (db alias, filters) when further constraining the fulfillment queryset rather than constructing a fresh queryset unless needed.
  - Extend the existing filter_fulfillments method to recognize a new warehouse field inside each fulfillment filter object. Within one fulfillment filter object, status/metadata/warehouse conditions must combine (logical AND). Across multiple fulfillment objects in the list, combine with OR semantics, then apply as an Exists subquery against orders (so that orders are included if any of their fulfillments match the composite conditions).

2) GraphQL schema:
- In saleor/graphql/schema.graphql:
  - Add a new input type FulfillmentWarehouseFilterInput with fields:
    - id: GlobalIDFilterInput
    - slug: StringFilterInput
    - externalReference: StringFilterInput
  - Extend FulfillmentFilterInput to include a new field:
    - warehouse: FulfillmentWarehouseFilterInput
  - Ensure descriptions categorize under Orders and match the style of existing schema descriptions.

3) Filter utilities typing:
- In saleor/graphql/utils/filters.py:
  - Broaden type hints for helper filter functions so they accept generic Mapping/Sequence rather than concrete dict/list, for:
    - filter_where_by_value_field: value parameter should support Mapping[str, scalar or Sequence of scalar]
    - filter_where_by_id_field: value parameter should support Mapping[str, str or list[str]]
  - No change in runtime behavior is required; only broadened typing/acceptance semantics.

4) Tests:
- In saleor/graphql/order/tests/queries/test_order_with_where.py:
  - Update the orders_with_fulfillments fixture to create:
    - Two Stocks for two different product variants, each in a distinct Warehouse.
    - One Fulfillment per order with FulfillmentLines pointing to those Stocks (no allocations needed for this test).
  - Add test cases that validate warehouse filtering inside where.fulfillments:
    - Filter by warehouse.id using eq and oneOf.
    - Filter by warehouse.slug using eq and oneOf.
    - Filter by warehouse.externalReference using eq and oneOf.
    - Verify that non-existing id/slug/externalReference inputs yield zero results.
    - Verify combining warehouse with additional fulfillment filters (status and metadata) both in matching and non-matching scenarios.
  - Use to_global_id_or_none when passing warehouse ids in variables.

5) Documentation note:
- In CHANGELOG.md under the section describing new order filters, add a bullet noting: "Filter by warehouse used to fulfill the order."

Behavioral expectations:
- The orders query, when provided with where.fulfillments containing a warehouse filter, returns only those orders that have at least one fulfillment line whose stock belongs to a warehouse matching the provided filters.
- Within a single where.fulfillments entry, the status, metadata, and warehouse constraints must all match (AND). When multiple entries are provided in the array, they are combined as OR.
- The new warehouse-based filter composes correctly with existing where-based filters for fulfillments and other order attributes.
- Empty or invalid warehouse filters result in no orders being returned for that particular fulfillment filter object.
- The schema changes expose the new input fields in a manner consistent with existing naming conventions (externalReference camelCase in schema; mapped to external_reference in model-level filters).

Extend the existing fulfillment filters in the orders where-based filtering so that a warehouse filter can be supplied with id, slug, or externalReference. Make sure this composes correctly with the existing fulfillment status and metadata filters and that it affects the orders query by including orders that have any fulfillment whose lines reference stock in warehouses matching the filter. Update the GraphQL schema to include a warehouse filter input for fulfillments, broaden the filter utility typings to accept mappings/sequences, and add tests that cover id, slug, externalReference, non-matching cases, and combinations with other fulfillment filters. Also update the changelog to mention this new filtering capability.

evalCommits.spec:
Implement reference-based attribute filtering for ProductVariant.where.attributes.reference.

Scope
- Add reference filtering helpers for AttributeValue lookups by referenced Page/Product/Variant identifiers.
- Extend variant attribute filtering to support reference filters (by page slugs, product slugs, variant skus, and global IDs for Page/Product/ProductVariant).
- Update validation to accept only correct reference inputs and reject empty/invalid combinations.
- Add tests that verify filtering semantics and validation errors.

Files to change
1) saleor/graphql/attribute/shared_filters.py
- Add helper functions to resolve AttributeValue by reference targets:
  - Internal generic helpers for pages/products/variants by identifier, then public wrappers:
    - get_attribute_values_by_referenced_page_slugs(slugs, db_connection_name) -> QuerySet[AttributeValue]
    - get_attribute_values_by_referenced_page_ids(ids, db_connection_name) -> QuerySet[AttributeValue]
    - get_attribute_values_by_referenced_product_slugs(slugs, db_connection_name) -> QuerySet[AttributeValue]
    - get_attribute_values_by_referenced_product_ids(ids, db_connection_name) -> QuerySet[AttributeValue]
    - get_attribute_values_by_referenced_variant_skus(slugs, db_connection_name) -> QuerySet[AttributeValue]
    - get_attribute_values_by_referenced_variant_ids(ids, db_connection_name) -> QuerySet[AttributeValue]
  - Each should query the referenced model (Page/Product/ProductVariant) using the given identifiers against the relevant field (slug/id/sku), and return AttributeValue filtered by Exists(...) where the AttributeValue.reference_*_id matches OuterRef on the referenced queryset.
- Ensure the CONTAINS_TYPING alias is available for import in product_variant filters: dict[Literal["contains_any","contains_all"], list[str]].
- Ensure validate_attribute_value_input already validates the 'reference' value input:
  - For attributes with input_type != REFERENCE, using 'reference' must be rejected.
  - For 'reference', accept only one of 'referencedIds', 'pageSlugs', 'productSlugs', 'productVariantSkus'. Inside each, accept only one of containsAll or containsAny, and arrays must be non-null and non-empty.
  - Raise GraphQLError messages aligned with tests when: value is empty/null, multiple keys provided, mismatched input types, both containsAll and containsAny provided, or contains* provided with empty list.

2) saleor/graphql/product/filters/product_variant.py
- Import typing.Literal.
- Import CONTAINS_TYPING and the new shared_filters getters for referenced pages/products/variants.
- Implement reference filter builders that return Q expressions:
  - _filter_contains_single_expression(attr_id, db_connection_name, referenced_attr_values):
    - Optionally restrict referenced_attr_values to the given attr_id.
    - Build Exists subquery checking AssignedVariantAttributeValue where value__in referenced_attr_values and assignment_id=OuterRef("id"); then wrap with Exists over AssignedVariantAttribute for the variant (variant_id=OuterRef("pk")).
  - filter_by_contains_referenced_page_slugs(attr_id, attr_value: CONTAINS_TYPING, db_connection_name):
    - For containsAll: AND multiple single expressions each built with a single slug;
      For containsAny: one expression over all slugs.
  - filter_by_contains_referenced_product_slugs(...): same pattern for products.
  - filter_by_contains_referenced_variant_skus(...): same pattern for variants.
  - filter_by_contains_referenced_object_ids(attr_id, attr_value: CONTAINS_TYPING, db_connection_name):
    - Decode global IDs using graphene.Node.from_global_id, bucket into page_ids, product_ids, variant_ids sets.
    - For containsAll: build AND expression requiring presence of each referenced object by ID using get_attribute_values_by_referenced_*_ids.
    - For containsAny: build OR expression across the groups using batched ID queries.
  - filter_objects_by_reference_attributes(attr_id, attr_value, db_connection_name): compose Q by intersecting (AND) results of any present keys among referencedIds, pageSlugs, productSlugs, productVariantSkus.
- Integrate into filter_variants_by_attributes:
  - When a given attribute filter has value.reference, apply attr_filter_expression &= filter_objects_by_reference_attributes(attr_id, attr_value["reference"], qs.db).
  - Keep existing behavior for slug/name, numeric, boolean, date, date_time unchanged.

3) Tests
- Modify saleor/graphql/product/tests/queries/variants_where/test_over_multiple_arguments.py
  - Add parameterized test test_product_variants_query_with_multiple_attribute_referenced_ids verifying containsAny yields 3 results and containsAll yields 1, using a mix of referenced Product, Page, and ProductVariant global IDs. Ensure combinations work across multiple attributes.
- Add new files and tests:
  - saleor/graphql/product/tests/queries/variants_where/test_over_references_pages.py
    - Tests for page reference by slug within a specific attribute slug and across attributes; validate containsAny and containsAll semantics and counts.
    - Tests for filtering by referencedIds (global IDs) within a page-reference attribute slug.
  - saleor/graphql/product/tests/queries/variants_where/test_over_references_products.py
    - Similar tests for product references by product slugs and by referencedIds.
  - saleor/graphql/product/tests/queries/variants_where/test_over_references_variants.py
    - Similar tests for variant references by productVariantSkus and by referencedIds.
- Update saleor/graphql/product/tests/queries/variants_where/test_over_validation.py
  - Extend invalid input cases to include various malformed 'reference' inputs:
    - Empty reference structures, None values, empty containsAll/containsAny arrays, providing both containsAll and containsAny, and using 'reference' with non-reference attributes. Ensure tests assert GraphQL errors and null data for productVariants as in the diff.

Behavioral requirements
- Filtering by attributes.value.reference applies regardless of whether the attribute slug is provided:
  - If slug is provided, restrict matching to that attribute; if not, match any attribute of input_type REFERENCE assigned to the variant.
- containsAll means the variant must have at least one assigned attribute value referencing each specified target (all of them), possibly across values and attributes; containsAny means the variant must have at least one assigned attribute value referencing any of the targets listed.
- For referencedIds, decode global IDs and support Page, Product, ProductVariant; ignore unsupported types.
- Performance: use Exists subqueries scoped to qs.db; do not fetch full rows; use .using(db_connection_name) for all queries.

Non-goals
- Do not change legacy ProductVariantFilterInput logic.
- Do not change other object filters (products/pages).

Validate the reference input so it rejects empty or malformed values and conflicting operators. Provide tests that cover reference filtering over pages, products, and variants, for both containsAny and containsAll, and tests that assert validation errors for invalid inputs.

evalCommits.spec:
Implement optional attribute slug in page where filtering and support value-only filters:

1) GraphQL schema input
- In saleor/graphql/schema.graphql, change AttributePageWhereInput.slug from required to optional (slug: String). Keep the existing description.
- Reflect the same in the Graphene class: in saleor/graphql/page/filters.py, class AttributePageWhereInput, set slug to required=False.

2) Filtering behavior when slug is omitted
- In saleor/graphql/page/filters.py, generalize all attribute-specific filter helpers to accept an optional attribute ID:
  - Update signatures to accept attr_id: int | None for: filter_by_slug_or_name, filter_by_numeric_attribute, filter_by_boolean_attribute, filter_by_date_attribute, filter_by_date_time_attribute.
  - When attr_id is provided, restrict AttributeValue queryset by attribute_id=attr_id. When attr_id is None, do not filter by attribute_id.
  - For type-specific filters (numeric/boolean/date/date_time), ensure the AttributeValue queryset additionally restricts by attribute__input_type matching the respective type.
  - Construct AssignedPageAttributeValue filtering using value__in=<prepared AttributeValue queryset> together with page_id=OuterRef("id"); wrap with Q(Exists(...)).

3) filter_pages_by_attributes to support value-only inputs
- In saleor/graphql/page/filters.py, adjust filter_pages_by_attributes(qs, value) to:
  - Build the attribute_slugs set only from inputs that include a slug key and fetch attributes_map from the DB for those slugs.
  - Handle inputs that provide a slug without a value as the “has any value assigned” case separately.
  - For each remaining input (including those without slug), branch based on which key is present inside "value": slug, name, numeric, boolean, date, date_time, or reference.
  - For each item, compute attr_id from attributes_map if slug present; otherwise attr_id=None. Pass attr_id to the respective helper (slug/name, numeric, boolean, date, date_time, reference) and combine all results with logical AND.
  - If no expression is built, return the original queryset; otherwise apply the combined filter.

4) Validation changes for attribute where inputs
- In saleor/graphql/page/filters.py, update validate_attribute_value_input to support optional slug and index-based error reporting:
  - Build slug_list only from entries that include a slug; still detect duplicate slugs and raise the existing duplicated-slug error.
  - Iterate inputs with their index; treat these as invalid and collect their positions: missing both slug and value; slug provided as null; value provided but empty or null.
  - For entries with a value, enforce that only one key is present inside value; otherwise collect the index for the "only one input key" error.
  - For type-specific validation, only validate the value key against attribute.input_type when a slug is present (build a mapping of slug -> (index, value_key) and fetch attributes by slug). If mismatched, collect the index for the type-mismatch error.
  - For reference values, collect (index, reference_dict) and pass to the reference validator.
  - Raise GraphQLError with updated messages that reference "positions" (indexes) instead of slugs for: empty/null value, multiple keys, and type mismatches, using the phrasing shown in the diff.

- Update validate_attribute_value_reference_input to accept a list of (index_str, reference_dict | None) and enforce:
  - If value is falsy/None, collect index in an "invalid input type" error that indicates a missing containsAll/containsAny key.
  - Disallow providing both containsAll and containsAny for the same reference target; collect index for a duplication error.
  - Disallow empty lists for containsAll/containsAny; collect index for an empty-value error.
  - Raise GraphQLError with messages referencing positions and following the updated phrasing.

5) Integration with where filterset
- Ensure PageWhere continues to:
  - Expose attributes as a ListObjectTypeWhereFilter(input_class=AttributePageWhereInput) that calls filter_pages_by_attributes.
  - Invoke validate_attribute_value_input in is_valid when attributes are present.

Acceptance criteria:
- The pages query supports where: { attributes: [{ value: { slug/name/numeric/boolean/date/dateTime/reference: ... } }] } without providing a slug and returns correct results by applying the value filter across attributes of matching input types.
- All basic value fields (name, slug) work with and without attribute slug; numeric/date/datetime/boolean value filters operate correctly including range and oneOf; reference filters support referencedIds, pageSlugs, productSlugs, productVariantSkus with containsAny/containsAll semantics.
- Validation errors reference input positions (indexes) and not slugs; messages match the updated phrasing for empty/null values, multiple value keys, type mismatches, and invalid reference inputs.
- Existing behavior with an explicit slug remains supported with no regressions.

When a slug is provided, filter within that attribute only; when omitted, apply the value filter across all attributes of the appropriate input type. Update validation to operate on list positions, reporting clear errors for empty inputs, multiple value keys, type mismatches, and malformed reference filters. Ensure the schema reflects the optional slug, helper filters and validators are updated accordingly, and that reference, numeric, boolean, date, dateTime, and basic name/slug filters all work with or without the attribute slug.

evalCommits.spec:
Implement productVariants filtering by associated attributes via GraphQL where filters.

Make the following changes:

1) saleor/graphql/attribute/shared_filters.py
- Import Number from ..utils/filters.
- Add helper functions that return QuerySet[AttributeValue] for reuse in variant filters without embedding assignment logic:
  - get_attribute_values_by_slug_or_name_value(attr_id: int|None, attr_value: dict, db_connection_name: str) -> QuerySet[AttributeValue]
    • If attr_id provided, scope to that attribute.
    • If attr_value contains slug and/or name, apply filter_where_by_value_field on those fields.
  - get_attribute_values_by_numeric_value(attr_id: int|None, numeric_value: dict[str, Number|list[Number]|dict[str, Number]], db_connection_name: str) -> QuerySet[AttributeValue]
    • Scope to AttributeInputType.NUMERIC and attr_id when provided.
    • Apply filter_where_by_numeric_field on the numeric field.
  - get_attribute_values_by_boolean_value(attr_id: int|None, boolean_value: bool, db_connection_name: str) -> QuerySet[AttributeValue]
    • Scope to AttributeInputType.BOOLEAN (and attr_id if provided) and filter boolean field equal to the provided value.
  - get_attribute_values_by_date_value(attr_id: int|None, date_value: dict[str, str], db_connection_name: str) -> QuerySet[AttributeValue]
    • Scope to AttributeInputType.DATE
    • Apply filter_range_field on "date_time__date".
  - get_attribute_values_by_date_time_value(attr_id: int|None, date_value: dict[str, str], db_connection_name: str) -> QuerySet[AttributeValue]
    • Scope to AttributeInputType.DATE_TIME
    • Apply filter_range_field on "date_time".
- Do not alter existing page/product assignment-specific filter helpers or validate_attribute_value_input; the new functions are additive and will be consumed by the variant filtering logic.

2) saleor/graphql/product/filters/product_variant.py
- Update imports:
  • Import QuerySet from django.db.models.query.
  • Import AssignedVariantAttribute, AssignedVariantAttributeValue, Attribute, AttributeValue from ....attribute.models.
  • Import AssignedAttributeWhereInput, validate_attribute_value_input and the new helper functions from ...attribute/shared_filters.
  • Import ListObjectTypeWhereFilter from ...core/filters.
  • Import Number from ...utils/filters.
- Implement helper function to turn AttributeValue queryset into a variant-level Q expression:
  • _get_assigned_variant_attribute_for_attribute_value_qs(attribute_values: QuerySet[AttributeValue], db_connection_name: str) -> Q
    – Build a subquery on AssignedVariantAttributeValue filtered by value__in attribute_values and assignment_id=OuterRef("id").
    – Exists over AssignedVariantAttribute with Exists(assigned_attr_value) and variant_id=OuterRef("pk").
- Implement filter helpers that use the new shared_filters getters and return Q via the above helper:
  • filter_by_slug_or_name(attr_id, attr_value, db_connection_name)
  • filter_by_numeric_attribute(attr_id, numeric_value, db_connection_name)
  • filter_by_boolean_attribute(attr_id, boolean_value, db_connection_name)
  • filter_by_date_attribute(attr_id, date_value, db_connection_name)
  • filter_by_date_time_attribute(attr_id, date_value, db_connection_name)
- Implement filter_variants_by_attributes(qs: QuerySet[ProductVariant], value: list[dict]) -> QuerySet[ProductVariant]
  • Resolve provided attribute slugs to Attribute records using qs.db; if any provided slug is not found, return qs.none().
  • Support two cases per input element: with slug and value, and with slug only (meaning: any value of that attribute).
  • For slug-only entries, gather all AttributeValue for those attributes and include variants having any of those values (via the assignment Q expression).
  • For entries with value: route to the appropriate filter based on key present in value (slug/name -> slug/name; numeric -> numeric; boolean -> boolean; date -> date; date_time -> dateTime). Combine conditions with AND across inputs.
  • Return qs.filter(combined_expression); if there is no condition, return qs (or qs.none() per original diff – follow the diff logic which returns qs.filter(expr)).
- Extend ProductVariantWhere:
  • Add attributes = ListObjectTypeWhereFilter(input_class=AssignedAttributeWhereInput, method="filter_attributes", help_text="Filter by attributes associated with the variant." + ADDED_IN_322)
  • Add filter_attributes(qs, _, value) to call filter_variants_by_attributes when value provided.
  • Override is_valid to call validate_attribute_value_input(self.data["attributes"], self.queryset.db) when attributes present, then super().is_valid().

3) saleor/graphql/schema.graphql
- In input ProductVariantWhereInput, add:
  """
  Filter by attributes associated with the variant.
  
  Added in Saleor 3.22.
  """
  attributes: [AssignedAttributeWhereInput!]
- Ensure AssignedAttributeWhereInput input type is defined once (move it above or reuse the existing definition) with fields:
  • slug: String
  • value: AssignedAttributeValueInput — description must state that only one value input field is allowed; providing more than one raises an error.
- Remove any duplicated AssignedAttributeWhereInput definition blocks from elsewhere in the schema file to avoid duplicates.

4) Tests – add new test suite for variants where attributes:
- Create directory saleor/graphql/product/tests/queries/variants_where/ with:
  • __init__.py (empty)
  • shared.py defining PRODUCT_VARIANTS_WHERE_QUERY: a query with variables where: ProductVariantWhereInput and channel.
  • test_over_attributes.py – tests variant query over attribute slug, value slug/name, with/without attribute slug provided, asserting counts and specific IDs.
  • test_over_attributes_boolean.py – tests boolean attributes across two attributes with slug and without, checking counts and specific id match.
  • test_over_attributes_date.py – tests date attribute filters using date range, name/slug matching, with and without explicit attribute slug; assert counts.
  • test_over_attributes_datetime.py – similar for dateTime field; include both with slug and without, test ranges and slug/name matching; assert counts.
  • test_over_attributes_numeric.py – tests numeric eq, oneOf, range, as well as name/slug string matching for numeric values; with and without explicit attribute slug; assert counts.
  • test_over_multiple_arguments.py – tests negative cases (non-matching attribute/value, multiple attributes with one non-existing) expecting 0 results and combination of multiple attributes expecting specific counts.
  • test_over_validation.py – tests various invalid inputs for type-specific mismatches, empty/null value, duplicated attr slug, multiple keys in value, and ensures GraphQL errors are returned and data.productVariants is None.
- Tests should use associate_attribute_values_to_instance from saleor.attribute.utils, get_graphql_content helper, and existing fixtures (e.g., staff_api_client, product_variant_list, weight_attribute, channel_USD, etc.). Names and shapes as in the diff to ensure compatibility with existing test fixtures.

5) CHANGELOG.md
- Under the relevant features section, add a bullet:
  - Add support for filtering `productVariants` by associated attributes

Acceptance criteria:
- GraphQL schema exposes ProductVariantWhereInput.attributes with help text and is included in introspection.
- Filtering productVariants works for slug/name/numeric/boolean/date/dateTime value filters and for slug-only (any value) conditions, combining inputs with AND semantics.
- Invalid inputs (null/empty values, multiple value keys, mismatched input type for attribute by slug, duplicated slugs) are rejected with GraphQL errors as validated by validate_attribute_value_input.

+    [
+        ({"slug": "date", "value": {"date": {"gte": "2021-01-01"}}}, 1),
+        ({"slug": "date", "value": {"name": {"eq": "date-name-1"}}}, 1),
+        ({"slug": "date", "value": {"slug": {"eq": "date-slug-1"}}}, 1),
+        (
+            {
+                "slug": "date",
+                "value": {"name": {"oneOf": ["date-name-1", "date-name-2"]}},
+            },
+            1,
+        ),
+        (
+            {
+                "slug": "date",
+                "value": {"slug": {"oneOf": ["date-slug-1", "date-slug-2"]}},
+            },
+            1,
+        ),
+        (
+            {
+                "slug": "date",
+                "value": {"date": {"gte": "2021-01-02", "lte": "2021-01-03"}},
+            },
+            1,
+        ),
+        ({"value": {"date": {"gte": "2021-01-01"}}}, 2),
+        ({"value": {"name": {"eq": "date-name-1"}}}, 1),
+        ({"value": {"slug": {"eq": "date-slug-1"}}}, 1),
+        ({"value": {"name": {"oneOf": ["date-name-1", "date-name-2"]}}}, 2),
+        ({"value": {"slug": {"oneOf": ["date-slug-1", "date-slug-2"]}}}, 2),
+        ({"value": {"date": {"gte": "2021-01-01", "lte": "2021-01-02"}}}, 1),
+    ],
+)
+def test_product_variants_query_with_attribute_value_date(
+    date_input,
+    expected_count,
+    staff_api_client,
+    product_variant_list,
+    date_attribute,
+    channel_USD,
+):
+    # given
+    product = product_variant_list[0].product
+    product_type = product.product_type
+
+    date_attribute.type = "PRODUCT_TYPE"
+    date_attribute.slug = "date"
+    date_attribute.save()
+
+    second_date_attribute = Attribute.objects.create(
+        slug="second_date",
+        name="Second date",
+        type=AttributeType.PRODUCT_TYPE,
+        input_type=AttributeInputType.DATE,
+    )
+    product_type.variant_attributes.add(date_attribute, second_date_attribute)
+
+    attr_value_1 = date_attribute.values.first()
+    attr_value_1.date_time = datetime.datetime(2021, 1, 3, tzinfo=datetime.UTC)
+    attr_value_1.name = "date-name-1"
+    attr_value_1.slug = "date-slug-1"
+    attr_value_1.save()
+
+    variant_1 = product_variant_list[0]
+    associate_attribute_values_to_instance(
+        variant_1, {date_attribute.pk: [attr_value_1]}
+    )
+
+    second_attr_value = second_date_attribute.values.create(
+        date_time=datetime.datetime(2021, 1, 2, tzinfo=datetime.UTC),
+        name="date-name-2",
+        slug="date-slug-2",
+    )
+
+    variant_2 = product_variant_list[1]
+    associate_attribute_values_to_instance(
+        variant_2, {second_date_attribute.pk: [second_attr_value]}
+    )
+
+    variables = {"where": {"attributes": [date_input]}, "channel": channel_USD.slug}
+
+    # when
+    response = staff_api_client.post_graphql(
+        PRODUCT_VARIANTS_WHERE_QUERY,
+        variables,
+    )

+        [{"value": {"name": {"eq": "Non-existing Name"}}}],
+        # Existing numeric attribute with out-of-range value
+        [{"slug": "count", "value": {"numeric": {"eq": 999}}}],
+        [{"value": {"numeric": {"eq": 999}}}],
+        # Existing boolean attribute with no matching boolean value
+        [{"slug": "boolean", "value": {"boolean": False}}],
+        [{"value": {"boolean": False}}],
+        # Multiple attributes where one doesn't exist
+        [
+            {"slug": "weight_attribute", "value": {"slug": {"eq": "cotton"}}},
+            {"slug": "non-existing-attr", "value": {"slug": {"eq": "some-value"}}},
+        ],
