+    product_type = product_variant_list[0].product.product_type
+    product_type.variant_attributes.set(
+        [
+            weight_attribute,
+            tag_attribute,
+            boolean_attribute,
+            numeric_attribute_without_unit,
+            date_attribute,
+            date_time_attribute,
+        ]
+    )
+
+    weight_value = weight_attribute.values.get(slug="cotton")
+    tag_value = tag_attribute.values.get(name="About")
+    boolean_value = boolean_attribute.values.filter(boolean=True).first()
+    numeric_value = numeric_attribute_without_unit.values.first()
+    date_time_value = date_time_attribute.values.first()
+    date_value = date_attribute.values.first()
+
+    date_attribute.slug = "date"
+    date_attribute.save()
+    date_time_attribute.slug = "date_time"
+    date_time_attribute.save()
+
+    associate_attribute_values_to_instance(
+        product_variant_list[0],
+        {
+            weight_attribute.pk: [weight_value],
+            tag_attribute.pk: [tag_value],
+            boolean_attribute.pk: [boolean_value],
+            numeric_attribute_without_unit.pk: [numeric_value],
+            date_attribute.pk: [date_value],

evalCommits.spec:
Refactor and centralize attribute filtering and validation logic into the shared attribute GraphQL module, and update page filters to delegate to it.

Make these changes:

1) saleor/graphql/attribute/shared_filters.py (add shared filtering and validation)
- Add imports: GraphQLError from graphql; AttributeInputType from saleor.attribute; and from ..utils.filters import filter_range_field, filter_where_by_numeric_field, filter_where_by_value_field.
- Implement model-agnostic filter builders that return filter expressions for use with QuerySet.filter, each accepting: attr_id (int|None), the value payload, db_connection_name, assigned_attr_model (e.g., AssignedPageAttributeValue), and assigned_id_field_name (e.g., "page_id"):
  • filter_by_slug_or_name(...): Build an AttributeValue queryset filtered by slug/name and optional attribute_id; build an Exists subquery over assigned_attr_model constrained by the assigned_id_field_name; return a filter expression to AND with Q objects.
  • filter_by_numeric_attribute(...): Limit AttributeValue to input_type NUMERIC and filter via filter_where_by_numeric_field on the "numeric" field; wrap with an Exists over assigned_attr_model; return a Q-compatible expression.
  • filter_by_boolean_attribute(...): Limit AttributeValue to input_type BOOLEAN and boolean value; wrap with Exists over assigned_attr_model; return a Q-compatible expression.
  • filter_by_date_attribute(...): Limit AttributeValue to input_type DATE and filter via filter_range_field on field "date_time__date"; wrap with Exists over assigned_attr_model; return a Q-compatible expression.
  • filter_by_date_time_attribute(...): Limit AttributeValue to input_type DATE_TIME and filter via filter_range_field on field "date_time"; wrap with Exists over assigned_attr_model and return a filter expression suitable for composition with other filters.
- Implement filtering for reference attributes by composing shared reference helpers already present in this module:
  • filter_objects_by_reference_attributes(attr_id, attr_value, db_connection_name, assigned_attr_model, assigned_id_field_name): Combine results of filter_by_contains_referenced_object_ids, filter_by_contains_referenced_pages, filter_by_contains_referenced_products, and filter_by_contains_referenced_variants based on keys present in attr_value ("referenced_ids", "page_slugs", "product_slugs", "product_variant_skus"). Return a combined Q expression.
- Implement a generic attribute filter orchestrator:
  • filter_objects_by_attributes(qs, value, assigned_attr_model, assigned_id_field_name):
    - Resolve provided attribute slugs to Attribute instances using qs.db. If any provided slug doesn’t exist, return qs.none().
    - If an entry contains only a slug (no value), include a condition that the entity has any value for that attribute (Exists over assigned attribute values).
    - For value-provided entries, detect which single key is present and combine corresponding filter expressions: slug/name (via filter_by_slug_or_name), numeric, boolean, date, date_time, or reference (via filter_objects_by_reference_attributes). Always use the db alias from qs.db and the provided assigned model/id field.
    - If any expressions were built, return qs.filter(combined_expression); otherwise return qs.none().
- Move and expose validation helpers (ensuring identical behavior/messages as previously in page filters):
  • validate_attribute_value_reference_input(index_with_values): Validate that each reference filter supplies exactly one of containsAll/containsAny, and that the lists are non-empty; raise GraphQLError using the same error messages, listing offending positions as comma-separated indices.
  • validate_attribute_value_input(attributes, db_connection_name): Validate the attribute where input list by enforcing: no duplicate slugs; slug cannot be null; value cannot be empty or null; value must contain only one key; when a type-specific value key (numeric, date, date_time, boolean, reference) is used alongside a slug, check the attribute’s input_type from the DB by slug; collect reference values and pass to validate_attribute_value_reference_input; raise GraphQLError with the same messages for each violation.
- Keep/define CONTAINS_TYPING = dict[Literal["contains_any", "contains_all"], list[str]] in this file for reference filters.

2) saleor/graphql/page/filters.py (delegate to shared filters)
- Remove locally defined attribute filter/validation functions and related imports (e.g., Literal, Exists, OuterRef, GraphQLError, AttributeInputType, Attribute, AttributeValue; and utilities no longer needed like filter_range_field and filter_where_by_numeric_field).
- Import from ..attribute.shared_filters: AssignedAttributeWhereInput, filter_objects_by_attributes, validate_attribute_value_input. Keep AssignedPageAttributeValue import.
- Replace filter_pages_by_attributes(qs, value) to return filter_objects_by_attributes(qs, value, AssignedPageAttributeValue, "page_id").
- In PageWhere (where filter class), keep metadata-related behavior, ensure filter_attributes returns filter_pages_by_attributes, and is_valid validates attributes via validate_attribute_value_input(attributes, self.queryset.db).

Behavioral requirements:
- Preserve previous functionality and error messages for attribute where input validation.
- Support filtering by slug/name equality/options, numeric ranges/equality/oneOf, boolean equality, date and datetime ranges, and reference attributes with containsAll/containsAny for pages, products, variants, and global IDs.
- Use the queryset’s db alias (qs.db) for all Attribute/AttributeValue/assigned model queries.
- The shared functions must be reusable by other entity types by passing their assigned attribute model and foreign key field name.

Validate the attribute where input consistently (no duplicate slugs, non-empty value with a single key, type-specific keys matching the attribute input type, and proper reference containsAll/containsAny semantics) and raise the same errors. Update the page where filter to import these helpers, delegate attribute filtering to the shared function, and call the shared validator in is_valid. Ensure all DB queries use the queryset’s db alias and that the refactor preserves existing behavior and results for attribute-based queries.

+                empty_input_value_error.add(index)

+            if (

+    if invalid_input_type_error:

+                invalid_input_type_list.append(index_str)

+                invalid_input_type_list.append(index_str)
+            if "reference" == value_key and input_type != AttributeInputType.REFERENCE:
+                invalid_input_type_list.append(index_str)

+                "Provided 'value' must have only one input key."

+        raise GraphQLError(
+            message=(
+                f"Incorrect input for attributes on position: {','.join(invalid_input_type_list)}. "

+from django.db import transaction
+from django.db.models import F, FloatField
+from django.db.models.functions import Cast
+
+from ....celeryconf import app
+from ....core.db.connection import allow_writer
+from ...models.base import AttributeValue
+
+# Takes around 0.11 seconds to process the batch.
+# The memory usage is marginal (~1MB).
+BATCH_SIZE = 500
+
+
+@app.task
+@allow_writer()
+def fulfill_attribute_value_numeric_field(attribute_value_pk=0):
+    value_ids = list(
+        AttributeValue.objects.filter(
+            pk__gte=attribute_value_pk,
+            numeric__isnull=True,
+            attribute__input_type="numeric",
+        )
+        .order_by("pk")
+        .values_list("id", flat=True)[:BATCH_SIZE]
+    )
+
+    if not value_ids:
+        return
+
+    with transaction.atomic():
+        locked_values = (
+            AttributeValue.objects.filter(id__in=value_ids)
+            .order_by("sort_order", "pk")
+            .select_for_update()
+            .values_list("id", flat=True)
+        )
+        AttributeValue.objects.filter(id__in=locked_values).update(
+            numeric=Cast(F("name"), FloatField())
+        )
+    fulfill_attribute_value_numeric_field.delay(value_ids[-1])

Implement dedicated, normalized storage for Adyen-specific transaction attributes and route them through the gateway response and persistence layer.

Scope and required changes:

1) Data contract: saleor/payment/interface.py
- In the GatewayResponse dataclass, add two optional string fields:
  - legacy_adyen_plugin_result_code
  - legacy_adyen_plugin_payment_method
- Keep raw_response but annotate with a deprecation comment indicating it is deprecated.

2) Persistence model: saleor/payment/models.py
- In the Transaction model, add two nullable TextField columns:
  - legacy_adyen_plugin_result_code = models.TextField(null=True)
  - legacy_adyen_plugin_payment_method = models.TextField(null=True)
- Add a model docstring/comment explaining these are temporary Adyen-only fields to support removing gateway_response later.
- Leave gateway_response as-is (JSONField) but mark it as deprecated via a comment.

3) Database migrations (new files):
- saleor/payment/migrations/0061_transaction_legacy_adyen_plugin_payment_method_and_more.py
  - Migration that adds the two new fields to the payment_transaction table (Transaction model).
- saleor/payment/migrations/0064_merge_20250716_0709.py
  - Merge migration that depends on 0061 above and an existing 0063 to resolve migration graph (use your repo’s latest numbers if they differ).

4) Transaction creation: saleor/payment/utils.py
- In create_transaction(), when constructing the Transaction instance, pass through the two new fields from the provided GatewayResponse to the Transaction model fields.
  - legacy_adyen_plugin_result_code=gateway_response.legacy_adyen_plugin_result_code
  - legacy_adyen_plugin_payment_method=gateway_response.legacy_adyen_plugin_payment_method

5) Adyen plugin behavior: saleor/payment/gateways/adyen/plugin.py
- Import logging and define logger = logging.getLogger(__name__).
- Add a helper method _normalize_response_field(field: str) -> str that returns field.strip().lower().
- Replace direct result.message["resultCode"].strip().lower() usages with self._normalize_response_field(result.message["resultCode"]).
- When creating GatewayResponse instances in these methods, populate the two new fields with normalized values (using the helper):
  - process_payment()
  - _process_additional_action()
  - confirm_payment() (the return path that builds GatewayResponse from existing transaction)
  - refund_payment()
  - capture_payment()
  - void_payment()
  Set:
    legacy_adyen_plugin_payment_method = normalized paymentMethod value from the Adyen response (default empty string if missing)
    legacy_adyen_plugin_result_code = normalized resultCode value from the Adyen response (default empty string if missing)
  Keep raw_response assigned to the raw Adyen response and annotate with a deprecation comment.
- In confirm_payment():
  - Read result_code from transaction.legacy_adyen_plugin_result_code if present; otherwise fallback to normalized transaction.gateway_response["resultCode"].
  - Read payment_method from transaction.legacy_adyen_plugin_payment_method if present; otherwise fallback to normalized transaction.gateway_response["paymentMethod"].
  - If both legacy fields are missing (i.e., both reads fell back), log a warning: "Reading deprecated raw_response from Adyen plugin.". Maintain existing logic around PENDING_STATUSES and AUTH_STATUS with iDEAL.

6) Adyen webhooks: saleor/payment/gateways/adyen/webhooks.py
- When creating GatewayResponse for create_new_transaction() and handle_api_response():
  - Populate legacy_adyen_plugin_payment_method and legacy_adyen_plugin_result_code with normalized (strip + lower) values derived from notification/response structures.
  - Keep raw_response as before and annotate with a deprecation comment.

7) Tests: saleor/payment/gateways/adyen/tests/test_plugin.py
- Update tests that create/compare expected GatewayResponse values to include the two new fields. For example, in test_process_additional_action expected GatewayResponse should include:
  - legacy_adyen_plugin_result_code set to normalized resultCode
  - legacy_adyen_plugin_payment_method set to normalized paymentMethod (empty string when not provided)

Acceptance criteria:
- All Adyen plugin and webhook-created GatewayResponse objects include the two legacy_adyen_plugin_* fields with normalized strings.
- Transaction records created from those responses persist these values in the new Transaction columns.
- confirm_payment() uses the new Transaction fields primarily, with a logged warning when falling back to deprecated gateway_response, and behavior remains consistent with previous logic.
- Database migrations apply cleanly and tests pass.

    - If metadata is provided: use filter_where_metadata on the same queryset.
  - For each constructed fulfillment_qs, AND into a cumulative lookup using Q(Exists(fulfillment_qs.filter(order_id=OuterRef("id")))) so all list items must be satisfied by at least one related fulfillment each.
  - If lookup is non-empty at the end, return qs.filter(lookup); otherwise return qs.none().

  - def filter_where_lines(qs, _, value: list | None):

  - Treat value as a list of input objects. For each input_data with metadata, build lines_qs = filter_where_metadata(OrderLine.objects.using(qs.db), None, metadata_value) and AND into lookup with Q(Exists(lines_qs.filter(order_id=OuterRef("id")))).

  - lines: change ObjectTypeWhereFilter to ListObjectTypeWhereFilter and update help_text similarly.

Each list item represents a group of conditions that must be satisfied by a single related object, and all provided groups must be satisfied across the related set (logical AND across list items). Update the filtering logic to iterate list items, build per-item subqueries using the existing helper filters and Exists, and combine them with AND. Update the GraphQL schema to change these fields to list input types and revise descriptions to explain the list semantics. Ensure empty or None inputs for these fields yield no results, and keep existing boolean flags like hasFulfillments and hasInvoices working as before.

evalCommits.spec:
Implement multi-transaction where filtering for orders and draft orders with list semantics and refactor transaction sub-filters to operate on TransactionItem querysets.

Update saleor/graphql/order/filters.py
- Imports:
  - Move Where-related filter classes and helpers to come from ..core.filters.where_filters. Keep non-where filters from ..core.filters.
  - Ensure the following are imported from ..core.filters.where_filters: BooleanWhereFilter, GlobalIDMultipleChoiceWhereFilter, ListObjectTypeWhereFilter, MetadataWhereBase, ObjectTypeWhereFilter, OperationObjectTypeWhereFilter, filter_where_metadata.
  - Ensure GlobalIDMultipleChoiceFilter, ListObjectTypeFilter, MetadataFilterBase, ObjectTypeFilter remain imported from ..core.filters.

- PaymentMethodDetailsFilterInput:
  - filter_card: Treat the incoming qs as a TransactionItem queryset. Return a filtered TransactionItem queryset where payment_method_type=PaymentMethodType.CARD; when brand is provided, use filter_where_by_value_field(transaction_qs, "cc_brand", brand_filter_value). Return the transaction queryset directly (do not wrap with order Exists here).
  - filter_type: Treat the incoming qs as a TransactionItem queryset. Use filter_where_by_value_field(qs, "payment_method_type", value) and return that transaction queryset directly (no Exists here).

- TransactionFilterInput:
  - filter_payment_method_details: The qs parameter denotes a TransactionItem queryset. Keep delegating to PaymentMethodDetailsFilterInput.filter_card/filter_type and return the TransactionItem queryset.
  - filter_metadata: Treat the incoming qs as a TransactionItem queryset and return filter_where_metadata(qs, None, value). Do not convert to an order queryset or wrap with Exists here.

- filter_where_transactions:
  - Change the input handling to expect a list of TransactionFilterInput items (list semantics). If not value (None or empty list), return qs.none().
  - For each list item (input_data), read input_data.get("metadata") and input_data.get("payment_method_details"). If both are missing/empty in any item, return qs.none().
  - For each item, build a transaction_qs starting from TransactionItem.objects.using(qs.db), applying TransactionFilterInput.filter_payment_method_details when present and TransactionFilterInput.filter_metadata when present. For that built transaction_qs, AND-accumulate onto a lookup as Q(Exists(transaction_qs.filter(order_id=OuterRef("id")))).
  - After processing all items, if any conditions were accumulated, return qs.filter(lookup); otherwise return qs.none().

- OrderWhere and DraftOrderWhere classes:
  - Replace transactions field from ObjectTypeWhereFilter to ListObjectTypeWhereFilter(input_class=TransactionFilterInput, method=filter_where_transactions).
  - Update help_text to describe the list semantics: each list item specifies conditions that must be satisfied by a single transaction; the filter matches orders having related objects meeting all groups of conditions.

Update saleor/graphql/schema.graphql
- In input OrderWhereInput and DraftOrderWhereInput:
  - Change transactions: TransactionFilterInput to transactions: [TransactionFilterInput!].
  - Update the field’s description to explain list semantics and matching behavior as above (a single transaction must satisfy each group; all groups required).

Update tests for orders and draft orders
- saleor/graphql/order/tests/queries/test_order_with_where.py and test_draft_order_with_where.py:
  - Update test cases to pass where inputs using a list for transactions, e.g., {"transactions": [{"paymentMethodDetails": {...}}, {"metadata": {...}}]}.
  - Where previous variables used {"where": {"transactions": where}}, change to passing the fully-formed where directly in variables = {"where": where} for the updated parameterizations.
  - Adapt metadata tests to accept lists of transaction filter items (e.g., [{"metadata": {...}}, {"metadata": {...}}]) and adjust expected results.
  - Add and verify new mixed-condition tests where list items mix metadata and payment method details and assert AND semantics across list items.

Acceptance behavior
- Orders/draftOrders where filter now supports: providing a list of TransactionFilterInput objects under transactions. The query returns orders that have, for each list item, at least one related TransactionItem satisfying that item’s conditions. If the transactions list is empty or an item lacks any supported fields, the result should be empty (qs.none()).
- Existing non-list order where fields must continue working as before.

      - Parse GraphQL global IDs to per-type ID sets for Page, Product, ProductVariant using graphene.Node.from_global_id.
      - If contains_all present: AND together conditions per type; if contains_any present: OR together conditions across types.
      - For each type, delegate to _filter_contains_all_condition/_filter_contains_any_condition with identifier_field_name="id" and attr_value_reference_field_name matching the AttributeValue FK field: reference_page_id, reference_product_id, reference_variant_id.
      - Return a Q expression.
    - Implement _filter_contains_single_expression(attr_id, db_connection_name, reference_objs QuerySet, attr_value_reference_field_name, assigned_attr_model, assigned_id_field_name):

    - Implement _filter_contains_all_condition(...) to AND per-identifier single-expression Qs where reference object is resolved by identifier_field_name value equals identifier.
    - Implement _filter_contains_any_condition(...) to OR matches by passing a single queryset resolved by identifier_field_name__in to _filter_contains_single_expression.
    - Implement wrappers for specific reference types that use slugs/SKUs:

      - filter_by_contains_referenced_products(...): identifier_field_name="slug", referenced_model=product_models.Product, attr_value_reference_field_name="reference_product_id".

    - productSlugs: ContainsFilterInput – Returns objects with a reference pointing to a product identified by the given slug.

5) Tests and fixtures
- File: saleor/graphql/page/tests/queries/test_pages.py

    - Filtering by referenced global IDs via referencedIds (containsAny/containsAll) for pages, variants, and products.

  - Ensure imports include AttributeValue and to_global_id_or_none and adjust any attribute slugs used in the tests per fixtures.

Acceptance criteria
- The pages(where: ...) filtering supports reference attribute values with containsAny/containsAll semantics via any of referencedIds, pageSlugs, productSlugs, productVariantSkus.
- Validation prevents null/empty ContainsFilterInput payloads and forbids mixing containsAny with containsAll for the same key.
- New ContainsFilterInput and ReferenceAttributeWhereInput are present in the schema; docs/descriptions reflect the above.

evalCommits.prompt:
Extend the Pages where filter to support filtering by reference attributes.

At a high level:
- Add an input for list-based membership checks with containsAny and containsAll.
- Support reference filters in pages where attributes so that clients can query by:
  - Global IDs of referenced objects
  - Page slugs
  - Product slugs
  - Variant SKUs
- For containsAll, only return pages that reference all specified items (AND semantics). For containsAny, return pages that reference at least one of them (OR semantics). Multiple keys can be combined and should all apply (AND between keys).
- Implement database-side filters using efficient Exists/OuterRef subqueries that resolve IDs, slugs, and SKUs for Page, Product, and ProductVariant references.
- Validate the where input: reject empty or null lists, and disallow providing both containsAny and containsAll for the same reference key. Also ensure the reference filter is only used for reference-type attributes.
- Update the GraphQL schema to include the new inputs and fields, and add tests for both happy-path and invalid inputs.

evalCommits.spec:
Implement a refactor and race-condition fix across payment transaction handling and related tests:

1) Centralize transaction processing helpers in payment.utils
- In saleor/payment/utils.py, expose two helpers:
  a) process_order_with_transaction(transaction, manager, user, app, previous_authorized_value=0, previous_charged_value=0, previous_refunded_value=0, related_granted_refund=None)
    • Lock the order and transaction using get_order_and_transaction_item_locked_for_update(order_id: UUID, transaction_pk)
    • Recalculate and update order amounts and statuses via updates_amounts_for_order(order, save=False), and set fields: total_charged_amount, charge_status, total_authorized_amount, authorize_status; save updated_at
    • If the channel automatically confirms new orders and the order is UNCONFIRMED, refresh_status and persist status
    • Update order search vector, fetch order info, and call order_transaction_updated with the previous_* values
    • If related_granted_refund given, recalculate its status
  b) process_order_or_checkout_with_transaction(transaction, manager, user, app, previous_authorized_value=0, previous_charged_value=0, previous_refunded_value=0, related_granted_refund=None)
    • If transaction.checkout_id is set: lock checkout and transaction using get_checkout_and_transaction_item_locked_for_update(checkout_id, transaction_pk), and update checkout amounts via transaction_amounts_for_checkout_updated_without_price_recalculation(transaction, checkout, manager, user, app). If checkout was deleted during processing, continue with order update if order_id exists
    • If transaction.order_id is set or checkout was deleted, call process_order_with_transaction() as above

- In saleor/payment/utils.py, update create_transaction_event_for_transaction_session() to call process_order_or_checkout_with_transaction(...) instead of inlined order/checkout update logic.

2) Remove duplicated helpers from GraphQL transaction utils
- In saleor/graphql/payment/mutations/transaction/utils.py, remove process_order_with_transaction and process_order_or_checkout_with_transaction definitions and their imports; keep get_transaction_item(...) and clean_customer_ip_address(...). Ensure remaining imports do not include checkout/order/payment locking or tracing utilities no longer used there.

3) Update GraphQL transaction mutations to import helpers from payment.utils
- In saleor/graphql/payment/mutations/transaction/transaction_create.py, import process_order_or_checkout_with_transaction from saleor.payment.utils and remove the import from .utils.
- In saleor/graphql/payment/mutations/transaction/transaction_event_report.py, import process_order_or_checkout_with_transaction from saleor.payment.utils and remove it from .utils.
- In saleor/graphql/payment/mutations/transaction/transaction_update.py, import process_order_or_checkout_with_transaction from saleor.payment.utils and remove it from .utils.

4) Avoid circular imports in order.actions
- In saleor/order/actions.py, move imports that create cycles inside functions:
  • In mark_order_as_paid_with_transaction, import create_transaction_for_order from ..payment.utils inside the function
  • In mark_order_as_paid_with_payment, import create_payment from ..payment.utils inside the function
  • In _process_refund, import refund from ..payment.gateway locally and call refund(...) instead of referring to a module-level payment.gateway import

5) Fix test patch targets and add coverage for locking and race condition

Goal: Remove race conditions and duplicated logic in GraphQL payment transaction mutations by introducing shared, lock-based processing helpers and refactoring mutations to use them. Update tests to target the new helpers and verify locking and race handling.

1) Shared helpers in saleor/graphql/payment/mutations/transaction/utils.py
- Add process_order_or_checkout_with_transaction(transaction, manager, user, app, previous_authorized_value=Decimal(0), previous_charged_value=Decimal(0), previous_refunded_value=Decimal(0), related_granted_refund=None) that:
  - If transaction.checkout_id exists: within traced_atomic_transaction, lock the checkout and the transaction via get_checkout_and_transaction_item_locked_for_update(checkout_id, transaction.pk); if locked checkout exists, update checkout payment statuses using transaction_amounts_for_checkout_updated_without_price_recalculation(transaction, locked_checkout, manager, user, app); otherwise mark checkout_deleted=True.
  - If transaction.order_id exists or checkout_deleted is True: call process_order_with_transaction(...) with the same transaction and previous_* values and optional related_granted_refund.
- Add process_order_with_transaction(transaction, manager, user, app, previous_authorized_value=Decimal(0), previous_charged_value=Decimal(0), previous_refunded_value=Decimal(0), related_granted_refund=None) that:
  - Within traced_atomic_transaction, lock the order and transaction via get_order_and_transaction_item_locked_for_update(order_id, transaction.pk), recompute and update order amounts/statuses (updates_amounts_for_order(order, save=False)) and set fields total_charged_amount, charge_status, total_authorized_amount, authorize_status. If channel.automatically_confirm_all_new_orders and order.status is UNCONFIRMED, refresh_order_status(order) and include status if changed. Save with updated_at.
  - After the transaction, update the order search vector (update_order_search_vector(order)), fetch order_info, and emit order_transaction_updated with previous_* values. If related_granted_refund is provided, recalculate its status (calculate_order_granted_refund_status).
- Ensure appropriate imports (User, App, Decimal, cast/UUID, traced_atomic_transaction, locking helpers, checkout actions, order utils/actions/search).

2) Refactor saleor/graphql/payment/mutations/transaction/transaction_create.py
- Remove class methods handling order/checkout processing and any imports used only by them.
- Import process_order_or_checkout_with_transaction from .utils and invoke it after creating the new transaction and recalculate_transaction_amounts(new_transaction). Do not pass money_data (defaults cover the behavior here).

3) Refactor saleor/graphql/payment/mutations/transaction/transaction_event_report.py
- Remove in-class processing methods and unused imports tied to them.
- Import and use process_order_or_checkout_with_transaction from .utils when amounts can be affected by the reported event, passing previous_authorized_value, previous_charged_value, previous_refunded_value, and related_granted_refund. Ensure app is typed App | None.

4) Refactor saleor/graphql/payment/mutations/transaction/transaction_update.py
- Remove duplicated update_order helper and direct order/checkout update logic (including previous_transaction_psp_reference comparison and manual search vector updates).
- After updating transaction fields and optionally creating an event, call process_order_or_checkout_with_transaction(instance, manager, user, app, previous_authorized_value, previous_charged_value, previous_refunded_value).
- Drop imports for checkout.actions.transaction_amounts_for_checkout_updated and other no-longer-used order utilities; import process_order_or_checkout_with_transaction from .utils instead.

5) Tests adjustments
- Update patch paths to target the helpers in utils:
  - test_transaction_create.py and test_transaction_event_report.py: patch saleor.graphql.payment.mutations.transaction.utils.get_order_and_transaction_item_locked_for_update and saleor.graphql.payment.mutations.transaction.utils.get_checkout_and_transaction_item_locked_for_update.
- In test_transaction_update.py:
  - Use checkout_with_prices instead of checkout_with_items where validating checkout status updates.

evalCommits.spec:
Implement per-channel control of releasing funds for expired checkouts and update all integration points.

1) Channel model (saleor/channel/models.py):
- Add fields to Channel:
  - release_funds_for_expired_checkouts: BooleanField, default False.
  - checkout_ttl_before_releasing_funds: DurationField, default 6 hours (timedelta(hours=6)).
  - checkout_release_funds_cut_off_date: DateTimeField, null=True, blank=True.
- Keep ordering and metadata intact.

2) Migrations (saleor/channel/migrations/):
- Create schema migration adding the three fields above. Additionally set DB defaults (via RunSQL) for zero-downtime:
  - checkout_ttl_before_releasing_funds default to interval 6 hours.
  - release_funds_for_expired_checkouts default to False.
- Create a data migration that batches through Channel rows and sets:
  - checkout_ttl_before_releasing_funds from settings.CHECKOUT_TTL_BEFORE_RELEASING_FUNDS.
  - release_funds_for_expired_checkouts to True if int(settings.TRANSACTION_BATCH_FOR_RELEASING_FUNDS) > 0, else False.
  - Only update rows where values differ. Use select_for_update in atomic transactions per batch.
- Add merge migrations to resolve graph conflicts if needed.

3) GraphQL API additions:
- Types (saleor/graphql/channel/types.py):
  - Extend PaymentSettings with:
    - releaseFundsForExpiredCheckouts: Boolean.
    - checkoutTtlBeforeReleasingFunds: Hour (integer hours).
    - checkoutReleaseFundsCutOffDate: DateTime.
  - Resolver for Channel.payment_settings must populate these fields; convert TTL timedelta to integer hours (seconds // 3600).
  - Ensure DateTime scalar is imported and used.
- Inputs (saleor/graphql/channel/mutations/channel_create.py and channel_update via shared input):
  - Extend PaymentSettingsInput with the same three fields and descriptions.
  - Ensure DateTime scalar is imported.
- Cleaning/validation (saleor/graphql/channel/mutations/utils.py):
  - Add clean_checkout_ttl_before_releasing_funds(hours: int) -> timedelta(hours=...); if value <= 0, raise ValidationError on field "checkoutTtlBeforeReleasingFunds" with code ChannelErrorCode.INVALID.
  - In clean_input_payment_settings, when provided:
    - Set release_funds_for_expired_checkouts directly.
    - Convert checkout_ttl_before_releasing_funds via the cleaner to timedelta and set on cleaned_input.
    - Pass checkout_release_funds_cut_off_date through to cleaned_input.

4) Periodic payment task (saleor/payment/tasks.py):
- Update transactions_to_release_funds() so that eligibility is controlled per checkout’s channel:
  - Only include checkouts whose channel has release_funds_for_expired_checkouts=True.
  - Enforce the channel-specific TTL for staleness: last_change older than now - channel.checkout_ttl_before_releasing_funds AND (last_transaction_modified_at is null OR it is older than now - channel.checkout_ttl_before_releasing_funds).
  - Enforce optional channel cut-off date: if checkout_release_funds_cut_off_date is set, only include checkouts with created_at strictly after that cut-off (checkouts created before cut-off are excluded).
  - Exclude checkouts older than one year (created_at <= now - 365 days) regardless of other conditions.
  - Implement the channel filter with an Exists() subquery correlated by checkout.channel_id and use OuterRef to reference checkout timestamps in comparisons. Preserve existing filters for authorize/charge status and automatically_refundable.

5) Tests:
- Channel fixtures (saleor/channel/tests/fixtures/channel.py): set release_funds_for_expired_checkouts=True for commonly used channels (e.g., USD and JPY fixtures) to enable test scenarios.
- GraphQL tests (saleor/graphql/channel/tests/mutations/):
  - Ensure channel create/update can set and returns releaseFundsForExpiredCheckouts, checkoutTtlBeforeReleasingFunds (integer hours), and checkoutReleaseFundsCutOffDate.
  - Add negative test: checkoutTtlBeforeReleasingFunds=0 returns INVALID error on the correct field.
- Payment tests (saleor/payment/tests/test_tasks.py):
  - Adjust previous TTL references to reflect a 6h default independent of the global setting.
  - Add tests verifying:
    - Only channels with release_funds_for_expired_checkouts enabled produce transactions to release.
    - Checkouts older than one year are excluded even if otherwise eligible.
- TransactionItem fixture (saleor/payment/tests/fixtures/transaction_item.py):
  - Allow passing currency as a parameter; default remains "USD"; stop hardcoding within the factory.

6) Schema file (saleor/graphql/schema.graphql):
- Update the SDL to expose the three new fields on PaymentSettings and PaymentSettingsInput, including descriptions and Added in 3.20 notes.

7) Scalars housekeeping (saleor/graphql/core/scalars.py):
- Ensure DateTime scalar is available to modules, and keep Hour and Day scalars exported; ordering of class definitions is not semantically important but keep them defined.

8) Operational: Ship migrations before code to ensure zero downtime. The Celery beat task should continue running with the new logic without relying on the old env-driven TTL/enablement.
evalCommits.prompt: Add per-channel controls for automatically releasing payment funds on expired checkouts and expose them via the Channel GraphQL API. Channels must be able to: enable or disable automatic release, configure a TTL in hours after the last change for releasing funds, and set an optional cut-off date after which expired checkouts are considered. Update the periodic task that gathers transactions to honor these per-channel settings, exclude checkouts older than a year, and apply the cut-off date when set. Extend the GraphQL payment settings (input and output), validate that TTL is positive, migrate existing channels from previous environment-based settings, and update tests to cover the new behavior.

Implement where and search support for filtering attribute choices on the Attribute.choices field.

Required changes:

1) Attribute values where filter and helper
- In saleor/graphql/attribute/filters.py:
  - Add a helper that filters AttributeValue by case-insensitive name/slug match using ilike OR logic (e.g., search_attribute_values). Ensure AttributeValueFilter.filter_search delegates to it for consistency.
  - Define AttributeValueWhere as a WhereFilterSet for AttributeValue with fields:
    - ids: list of Global IDs (GlobalIDMultipleChoiceWhereFilter) using filter_by_ids("AttributeValue").
    - name: OperationObjectTypeWhereFilter with StringFilterInput -> use filter_where_by_value_field for name.
    - slug: OperationObjectTypeWhereFilter with StringFilterInput -> use filter_where_by_value_field for slug.
    - Meta.model = AttributeValue, Meta.fields = [].
  - Define AttributeValueWhereInput (WhereInputObjectType) for AttributeValueWhere with doc_category set to attributes.

2) GraphQL field arguments and resolver
- In saleor/graphql/attribute/types.py:
  - Update Attribute.choices field definition to:
    - Keep existing sort_by argument.
    - Keep filter argument but mark it as deprecated in the description, explicitly instructing to use where instead (use DEPRECATED_IN_3X_INPUT).
    - Add where: AttributeValueWhereInput with description including ADDED_IN_322.
    - Add search: String argument with description including ADDED_IN_322.
  - In resolve_choices:
    - Preserve existing queryset selection behavior (return values only for attributes with input types supporting choices, else empty qs).
    - If a search argument is provided, apply name/slug ilike filtering via the new helper before passing through filter_connection_queryset.
    - Wrap qs with ChannelQsContext and pass kwargs through filter_connection_queryset to support filter/where mutual exclusivity and normal connection processing.

3) Schema updates
- In saleor/graphql/schema.graphql:
  - Under type Attribute, update choices:
    - filter: AttributeValueFilterInput marked deprecated with reason "Use where filter instead.".
    - where: AttributeValueWhereInput with documentation that it was added in Saleor 3.22.
    - search: String with documentation that it was added in Saleor 3.22.
  - Add input AttributeValueWhereInput with fields: ids: [ID!], name: StringFilterInput, slug: StringFilterInput, and automatically include AND, OR per WhereInputObjectType.

4) Tests for attribute choices filtering
- In saleor/graphql/attribute/tests/queries/test_attribute_where.py:
  - Add a query to fetch attribute(id) { choices(first: 10, where: $where, search: $search) { edges { node { name slug }}} }.
  - Add tests that create multiple AttributeValue instances for a given attribute and validate filtering by:
    - where.ids (by global IDs)
    - where.slug (eq and oneOf)
    - where.name (eq and oneOf)
    - search (free-text across name/slug)
  - Import AttributeValue where needed and reuse get_graphql_content helpers.

5) Changelog
- Update CHANGELOG.md to note: "You can now filter and search attribute choices using the new where and search fields on the attribute.choices query."

Behavioral requirements and constraints:
- Only one of filter or where can be provided on the Attribute.choices connection; both together must raise a GraphQL error (handled by filter_connection_queryset).
- Search is independent and applies a case-insensitive name/slug match prior to where/filter computation.
- Where filters must follow core where patterns, support nested AND/OR, and enforce single-option per operation (e.g., eq XOR oneOf) via DefaultOperationField.
- Follow existing doc_category, ADDED_IN_322, and DEPRECATED_IN_3X_INPUT conventions.
- Maintain and pass channel context through ChannelQsContext for nested connections and pagination.

Scope and requirements:

1) Wrap attribute nodes and querysets in channel context
- In saleor/graphql/attribute/schema.py:
  - Wrap the attributes list queryset in ChannelQsContext before returning through create_connection_slice.
  - For resolve_attribute, wrap the resolved model in ChannelContext(node=attribute, channel_slug=None); return None if not found.

2) Use channel-aware GraphQL types for attributes and values
- In saleor/graphql/attribute/types.py:
  - Change AttributeValue to inherit from ChannelContextType[AttributeValue] and set Meta.default_resolver = ChannelContextType.resolver_with_context.
  - Update all AttributeValue field resolvers to accept ChannelContext[models.AttributeValue] as root, refer to root.node, and propagate root.channel_slug when wrapping referenced objects or building File/IDs. Ensure TranslationField for AttributeValue uses resolver=ChannelContextType.resolve_translation.
  - Change Attribute to inherit from ChannelContextType[Attribute] and set Meta.default_resolver = ChannelContextType.resolver_with_context.
  - Update Attribute resolvers (choices, valueRequired, visibility flags, storefrontSearchPosition, availableInGrid, withChoices, productTypes, productVariantTypes) to accept ChannelContext[models.Attribute] as root and use root.node for data access. For choices, wrap the underlying AttributeValue queryset with ChannelQsContext(channel_slug=root.channel_slug) and pass that through filter_connection_queryset and create_connection_slice.
  - Change SelectedAttribute to subclass ChannelContextTypeForObjectType so its fields can accept ChannelContext-wrapped attribute/value nodes.

3) Update attribute mutations to return ChannelContext-wrapped payloads
- In saleor/graphql/attribute/mutations/attribute_create.py and attribute_update.py: return AttributeCreate/Update(attribute=ChannelContext(instance, None)).
- In attribute_reorder_values.py: return AttributeReorderValues(attribute=ChannelContext(attribute, None)).

- In attribute_value_create.py: return attribute and attributeValue wrapped with ChannelContext(..., None) in the mutation response.

Align page and product attribute resolvers to emit SelectedAttribute objects whose attribute and values are channel-wrapped, and make attribute connections use a channel-aware queryset wrapper. Update permission checks and metadata mutations so they work with channel-wrapped attribute nodes. Keep the public GraphQL API schema and field names stable while changing the internal resolution to be channel-aware, and update tests accordingly.

evalCommits.spec:
Implement channel-aware Page GraphQL behavior across the schema.

Scope and required changes:

1) Page type becomes channel-aware
- File: saleor/graphql/page/types.py
  - Change Page to inherit from ChannelContextType instead of ModelObjectType.
  - Set Meta.default_resolver to ChannelContextType.resolver_with_context.
  - Update translation field for Page to use resolver=ChannelContextType.resolve_translation.
  - Update all Page field resolvers to accept ChannelContext[models.Page] as root:
    - resolve_publication_date, resolve_created, resolve_page_type, resolve_content_json should use root.node instead of root, and where applicable load via root.node IDs.
    - In resolve_attributes and resolve_attribute:
      - Use page = root.node and wrap returned Attribute and AttributeValue objects in ChannelContext with channel_slug=root.channel_slug when building SelectedAttribute structures.
      - Ensure dataloaders use page.id, not root.id.

2) Page queries wrap nodes and querysets with channel context
- File: saleor/graphql/page/schema.py
  - resolve_page: Wrap the resolved page with ChannelContext(page, channel_slug=None); return None if not found.
  - resolve_pages: Wrap the queryset with ChannelQsContext(qs, channel_slug=None) before filter_connection_queryset/create_connection_slice.

3) MenuItem.page returns channel-aware Page
- File: saleor/graphql/menu/types.py
  - In MenuItem.resolve_page, when a page is loaded by PageByIdLoader:
    - Apply existing requestor permission/is_visible logic.
    - If allowed, return ChannelContext(node=page, channel_slug=root.channel_slug); otherwise return None.

4) AttributeValue.referenced_object wraps Page with ChannelContext
- File: saleor/graphql/attribute/types.py
  - In AttributeValue.resolve_referenced_object, for AttributeEntityType.PAGE, change the loader chain to PageByIdLoader(...).load(reference_pk).then(wrap_with_channel_context), using the same wrap_with_channel_context closure used for other entities and passing root.channel_slug.

5) Mutations return ChannelContext-wrapped Page in payloads
- File: saleor/graphql/page/mutations/page_create.py
  - Import ChannelContext and override success_response to assign response.page = ChannelContext(instance, channel_slug=None).
- File: saleor/graphql/page/mutations/page_update.py
  - Import ChannelContext and override success_response similarly as PageCreate; response.page must be ChannelContext(instance, channel_slug=None).
- File: saleor/graphql/page/mutations/page_delete.py
  - Import ChannelContext and after calling plugin event, set response.page = ChannelContext(page, channel_slug=None) before returning.
- File: saleor/graphql/page/mutations/page_reorder_attribute_values.py
  - Import ChannelContext and make perform_mutation return PageReorderAttributeValues(page=ChannelContext(page, channel_slug=None)).

6) Metadata base mutation recognizes Page as channel-aware
- File: saleor/graphql/meta/mutations/base.py
  - Import page_models.
  - Include page_models.Page in the isinstance union that triggers wrapping the instance with ChannelContext(node=instance, channel_slug=None) in success_response.

7) Translations return channel-aware Page on nested page field
- File: saleor/graphql/translations/types.py
  - In PageTranslatableContent.resolve_page, after fetching the page visible to the user, return ChannelContext(page, channel_slug=None) or None if not found.

8) Webhook subscription payloads return channel-aware Page
- File: saleor/graphql/webhook/subscription_types.py
  - In PageBase.resolve_page, wrap the page with ChannelContext(page, channel_slug=None).

Acceptance criteria:
- All resolvers returning a Page node directly return ChannelContext-wrapped nodes.
- All connections returning Page lists propagate ChannelContext via ChannelQsContext so edges’ nodes are wrapped with the provided channel_slug.
- SelectedAttribute structures in Page resolvers propagate the same channel context to embedded Attribute and AttributeValue.
- MenuItem.page and AttributeValue.referenced_object (for PAGE reference) return ChannelContext-wrapped pages.
- Mutations (create/update/delete/reorder attribute values) expose ChannelContext-wrapped Page in their response objects.
- Base metadata mutation wraps Page instances as channel-aware, consistent with other channel entities.
- Translations and webhook subscription types return ChannelContext-wrapped Pages.
- Behavior matches patterns used by Product/Collection channel context handling.

Implement a refactor to consolidate database row-locking helpers that use Django’s select_for_update into dedicated lock_objects.py modules per app, and update all call sites to use them. Specifically:

Create new lock_objects modules and functions
- saleor/checkout/lock_objects.py
  - Define checkout_qs_select_for_update() that returns a queryset for Checkout ordered by pk with select_for_update applied to self.
  - Define checkout_lines_qs_select_for_update() that returns a queryset for CheckoutLine ordered by pk with select_for_update applied to self.

- saleor/order/lock_objects.py
  - Define order_qs_select_for_update() that returns a queryset for Order ordered by pk with select_for_update applied to self.
  - Define order_lines_qs_select_for_update() that returns a queryset for OrderLine ordered by pk with select_for_update applied to self.

- saleor/payment/lock_objects.py
  - Define transaction_item_qs_select_for_update() that returns a queryset for TransactionItem ordered by pk with select_for_update applied to self.
  - Define get_order_and_transaction_item_locked_for_update(order_id, transaction_item_id) that locks and returns the specified Order and TransactionItem; acquire locks using the per-app helpers in a consistent order (Order, then TransactionItem).
  - Define get_checkout_and_transaction_item_locked_for_update(checkout_id, transaction_item_id) that locks and returns the specified Checkout (or None if not found) and TransactionItem; acquire locks using the per-app helpers in a consistent order (Checkout, then TransactionItem).

- saleor/warehouse/lock_objects.py
  - Define stock_select_for_update_for_existing_qs(qs) that orders by pk and applies select_for_update to self on the provided queryset.
  - Define stock_qs_select_for_update() that returns Stock queryset via stock_select_for_update_for_existing_qs(Stock.objects.all()).
  - Define allocation_with_stock_qs_select_for_update() that returns Allocation queryset with select_related("stock"), applies select_for_update to self and stock, and orders by stock__pk.

Remove old helper definitions from prior locations
- Remove checkout_lines_qs_select_for_update() from saleor/checkout/utils.py (and any associated unused imports).
- Remove order_qs_select_for_update() and order_lines_qs_select_for_update() from saleor/order/utils.py.
- Remove stock_select_for_update_for_existing_qs, stock_qs_select_for_update, and allocation_with_stock_qs_select_for_update from saleor/warehouse/management.py.

Update imports and call sites to use the new lock_objects helpers
- saleor/discount/utils/order.py: import order_qs_select_for_update from .../order/lock_objects instead of dynamically importing from order.utils; remove local/import-time indirections.
- saleor/discount/utils/promotion.py: import checkout_lines_qs_select_for_update from .../checkout/lock_objects and order_lines_qs_select_for_update from .../order/lock_objects; remove local imports inside functions.
- saleor/graphql/product/bulk_mutations/product_variant_bulk_delete.py: import order_lines_qs_select_for_update from .../order/lock_objects (not from order.utils).
- saleor/graphql/warehouse/bulk_mutations/stock_bulk_update.py: import stock_qs_select_for_update from .../warehouse/lock_objects (not from warehouse.management).
- saleor/order/actions.py: import order_lines_qs_select_for_update from .../order/lock_objects (not from order.utils).
- saleor/warehouse/reservations.py: import stock_qs_select_for_update from .../warehouse/lock_objects; keep sort_stocks import from management.
- saleor/graphql/payment/mutations/transaction/transaction_event_report.py:
  - Replace direct select_for_update locking of Order and TransactionItem with the new get_order_and_transaction_item_locked_for_update() helper.
  - Replace direct select_for_update locking of Checkout and TransactionItem with the new get_checkout_and_transaction_item_locked_for_update() helper.
  - Where only a TransactionItem lock is needed, use transaction_item_qs_select_for_update() instead of inlined select_for_update calls.

Documentation
- Update CONTRIBUTING.md by adding a "Locking Objects" section that explains:
  - Use select_for_update on querysets to lock rows.
  - Lock multiple objects in a consistent order (e.g., by pk) and define a cross-model lock acquisition order (e.g., Order before OrderLine).
  - Encapsulate locking logic in helper functions within lock_objects.py in the app directory of the model being locked. For multi-model locks, place the helper in the directory of the last model being locked, and document examples (e.g., Order then TransactionItem, helper in payment/lock_objects.py).

Behavioral/structural expectations
- All lock helper querysets must order by pk and scope select_for_update to self (and to related objects when specified) to reduce deadlock probability and clearly document lock scope.
- Combined helpers in payment must return locked instances within an atomic transaction context in callers; they themselves provide the row-level locking querysets and retrieval.
- All call sites should import helpers from lock_objects modules, not from utils.py or management.py.
- Type hints should reference concrete models via QuerySet[Model] where helpers return querysets.

Acceptance criteria
- All references to the old helper locations are removed and replaced with imports from the new lock_objects modules.
- The new helpers exist with the specified names and semantics in each app’s lock_objects.py.
- GraphQL transaction_event_report uses the new payment lock helpers and transaction_item_qs_select_for_update.
- CONTRIBUTING.md contains the new locking guidance section.
- No direct select_for_update sequences remain at updated call sites where a helper exists; they use the standardized helpers instead.

+### Locking Objects
+
+To lock objects and prevent race conditions in concurrent operations, use Django's [`select_for_update()`](https://docs.djangoproject.com/en/stable/ref/models/querysets/#select-for-update) method on querysets.
+
+#### General Guidelines
+
+- When locking **multiple objects**, always lock them **in a consistent order** to avoid deadlocks.
+  - Use a clear and stable ordering—typically by `pk`.
+  - When locking **across multiple models**, always acquire locks in a defined order. For example, lock the `Order` model **before** `OrderLine`.
+
+#### Best Practices
+
+To reduce the chance of deadlocks and to keep the locking logic consistent:
+
+- Wrap all locking logic in **helper functions**.
+- Place these helper functions in a file named `lock_objects.py` located in the same app directory as the model you're locking.
+  - For single-model locks, use the model's app directory (e.g. `orders/lock_objects.py`).
+  - For multi-model locks, place the function in the directory of the **last model being locked**.
+    - Example: If locking `Order` and `TransactionItem`, and `TransactionItem` is locked last, use `payment/lock_objects.py`.
+
 ### Searching
 
 So far, we have mainly used the `GinIndex` and `ilike` operators for searching, but currently, we are testing a new solution with the use of `SearchVector` and `SearchRank`.
 You can find it in this PR [#9344](https://github.com/saleor/saleor/pull/9344).

evalCommits.spec:
Implement concurrency-safe updates for payment transactions affecting checkouts and orders, add status refresh logic, and align tests.

Scope and behavioral requirements
- TransactionCreate mutation must update checkout and/or order amounts and statuses in a race-condition-safe way by locking the relevant rows in a single atomic section and by avoiding unintended price recalculations during the lock.
- TransactionEventReport’s order path must also lock and update within a traced atomic transaction based on the immutable identifiers, not ORM object references that can become stale.
- Order status recalculation must be factored into a reusable function that returns whether the status changed, and update_order_status should rely on it while ensuring locking and consistent persistence.
- Tests must assert that the correct “select_for_update” locking helpers are invoked within database transactions and verify the expected statuses in normal and race-condition scenarios.

Required changes by file
1) saleor/graphql/payment/mutations/transaction/transaction_create.py
- Add helper method process_order_with_transaction(transaction, manager, user, app, money_data) that:
  - Locks the order and the TransactionItem together using get_order_and_transaction_item_locked_for_update inside traced_atomic_transaction.
  - When money_data is provided, recompute order amounts with updates_amounts_for_order (no save) and collect update fields for total_authorized_amount, total_charged_amount, authorize_status, charge_status.
  - If the channel auto-confirms new orders and the order is UNCONFIRMED, refresh the order status using refresh_order_status and include status in update fields if it changed.
  - Save the locked order with update_fields + updated_at.
  - After the transaction, update the order’s search vector (non-atomic) and emit order_transaction_updated with previous_* values set to zero.
- Add helper method process_order_or_checkout_with_transaction(transaction, manager, user, app, money_data) that:
  - If the transaction has a checkout_id and money_data, lock the Checkout and TransactionItem together using get_checkout_and_transaction_item_locked_for_update inside traced_atomic_transaction. If the checkout still exists, update checkout payment statuses via transaction_amounts_for_checkout_updated_without_price_recalculation using the locked checkout instance; otherwise, flag that the checkout was deleted mid-process.
  - If the transaction has an order_id or the checkout was deleted, call process_order_with_transaction.
- Replace prior direct calls to transaction_amounts_for_checkout_updated and direct order updates in perform_mutation with a single call to process_order_or_checkout_with_transaction after recalculate_transaction_amounts.
- Update imports accordingly: TYPE_CHECKING, UUID, User, App, traced_atomic_transaction, get_checkout_and_transaction_item_locked_for_update, get_order_and_transaction_item_locked_for_update, refresh_order_status, updates_amounts_for_order.

2) saleor/graphql/payment/mutations/transaction/transaction_event_report.py
- Ensure the order-processing path locks the Order and TransactionItem by ID within traced_atomic_transaction:
  - Cast transaction.order_id to UUID and call get_order_and_transaction_item_locked_for_update(order_id, transaction.pk).
  - Recompute order amounts (updates_amounts_for_order) within the lock, then update_order_search_vector after the transaction and proceed with webhooks/events as before.
- Normalize type hints for user to User | None and fix TYPE_CHECKING import paths.

3) saleor/graphql/payment/mutations/transaction/transaction_update.py
- Provide a temporary update_order(order, money_data, update_search_vector=True) method (not yet refactored to the new helpers) that:
  - When money_data is provided, recomputes order amounts (updates_amounts_for_order with save=False) and includes total_authorized_amount, total_charged_amount, authorize_status, charge_status among update fields.
  - Auto-confirms by calling update_order_status if the channel requires and the order is UNCONFIRMED.
  - Optionally updates the order’s search vector (save=False) and appends search_vector to update_fields; save with updated_at.
- Add a TODO comment referencing planned refactor to use the new helper flow.

4) saleor/order/utils.py
- Add refresh_order_status(order) that recalculates the order status based on the latest fulfillment/returns/replacements quantities using existing helpers, returns True if status changed, False otherwise, and does not save. Document that it must be used with a locked order inside a transaction.
- Update update_order_status(order) to:
  - Open an atomic block and lock the order via select_for_update.
  - Call refresh_order_status(locked_order) and if status changed, save locked_order with status and updated_at.
  - Mirror the new status back to the original order instance so that callers see the updated status in their response.

5) Tests updates
- saleor/graphql/payment/tests/mutations/test_transaction_create.py
  - Replace fixtures that relied on checkout_with_items with checkout_with_prices where totals need to be present.
  - Add a test that patches get_order_and_transaction_item_locked_for_update to assert it’s called inside an atomic transaction when creating a transaction that updates order amounts; assert resulting full statuses and totals.
  - Add a test that patches get_checkout_and_transaction_item_locked_for_update to assert it’s called when creating a transaction that updates checkout amounts; assert resulting checkout statuses.
  - Add a race-condition test that triggers checkout completion concurrently (via race_condition.RunBefore wrapping recalculate_transaction_amounts) and assert that after the mutation the order exists with UNFULFILLED status, FULL authorize status, and NONE charge status.
- saleor/graphql/payment/tests/mutations/test_transaction_event_report.py
  - Use model enums OrderChargeStatus and OrderAuthorizeStatus (from saleor.order) instead of GraphQL enums for assertions.
  - Where appropriate, assert both charge and authorize statuses after updates, and maintain existing webhook assertions.

Acceptance criteria
- Creating or reporting a transaction event updates the checkout/order amounts and statuses without data races when the checkout is converted to an order concurrently.
- For checkout updates inside TransactionCreate, payment statuses are updated without recalculating prices during the lock and webhooks behave as before.
- Order updates lock the order + TransactionItem, refresh status only when needed, persist changes, and update the search vector afterward.
- update_order_status persists via the locked instance and keeps the caller’s in-memory order status in sync.
- All updated tests pass, including those asserting that the locking helpers were called, and the race-condition scenarios produce the expected statuses.
evalCommits.prompt: Improve the payment transaction mutations to be safe under concurrency and prevent race conditions when a checkout might be converted to an order during the mutation. Update the transaction creation flow to lock and update either the checkout or the order (and its transaction item) inside a single atomic block, refresh order status only when needed, and avoid unnecessary price recalculation for checkouts during the lock. Adjust the order status utilities to provide a lock-friendly status refresh and ensure the caller’s order object reflects the new status. Update tests to assert that the locking paths are exercised and that race conditions yield the expected order and checkout statuses.

The method must filter variants by the exact value(s) using filter_where_by_value_field on the sku field and support eq, oneOf, and notOneOf semantics; return an empty queryset when value is None or invalid.

The method must filter variants by a gte/lte range using filter_where_by_range_field on the updated_at field; return an empty queryset when value is None or when both gte and lte are missing.

evalCommits.spec:
- Add GraphQL filtering for orders by payment method details.

1) GraphQL enums
- In saleor/graphql/payment/enums.py, expose PaymentMethodType as a GraphQL enum named PaymentMethodTypeEnum with the payments doc category.

2) GraphQL inputs and where filters
- In saleor/graphql/order/filters.py:
  - Import PaymentMethodType and TransactionItem models alongside existing imports.
  - Import PaymentMethodTypeEnum from saleor/graphql/payment/enums.
  - Define PaymentMethodTypeEnumFilterInput with fields eq and one_of for PaymentMethodTypeEnum values.
  - Define PaymentMethodDetailsCardFilterInput with a StringFilterInput brand field ("Filter by payment method brand used to pay for the order.").
  - Define PaymentMethodDetailsFilterInput with fields:
    - type: PaymentMethodTypeEnumFilterInput ("Filter by payment method type used to pay for the order.")
    - card: PaymentMethodDetailsCardFilterInput ("Filter by card details used to pay for the order. Skips `type` filter if provided.")
  - Implement static filtering helpers on PaymentMethodDetailsFilterInput:
    - filter_card(qs, _, value): restrict to orders having at least one TransactionItem of payment_method_type=CARD; when a brand filter is provided, apply it against TransactionItem.cc_brand using the existing filter_where_by_value_field helper; correlate TransactionItem.order_id to Order.id via Exists/OuterRef.
    - filter_type(qs, _, value): apply filter_where_by_value_field to TransactionItem.payment_method_type and correlate to Order by Exists/OuterRef.
  - Define TransactionFilterInput with field payment_method_details: PaymentMethodDetailsFilterInput and implement filter_payment_method_details to dispatch to the appropriate helper. If both card and type are provided, card takes precedence.
  - Extend OrderWhere with a new ObjectTypeWhereFilter field transactions using TransactionFilterInput and implement filter_transactions that delegates to TransactionFilterInput.filter_payment_method_details when provided.

3) Schema additions
- In saleor/graphql/schema.graphql, add the following under Orders:
  - New input TransactionFilterInput with paymentMethodDetails.
  - New input PaymentMethodDetailsFilterInput with type and card sub-inputs.
  - New input PaymentMethodTypeEnumFilterInput with eq and oneOf.
  - New input PaymentMethodDetailsCardFilterInput with brand.
  - New enum PaymentMethodTypeEnum with CARD and OTHER values and a docstring reflecting the possible types.
  - Add transactions: TransactionFilterInput to OrderWhereInput with appropriate description.

4) Django model indexes
- In saleor/payment/models.py, extend TransactionItem.Meta.indexes to include BTree indexes for payment_method_type and cc_brand (names: payment_method_type_ids and cc_brand_idx). Keep existing indexes intact.
- Create a new migration saleor/payment/migrations/0063_transactionitem_payment_method_type_ids_and_more.py using AddIndexConcurrently to add the two BTree indexes for TransactionItem (atomic=False). Ensure proper dependencies on the prior payment migration that introduced the fields and other required apps.

5) Tests and fixtures
- Update saleor/payment/tests/fixtures/transaction_item.py transaction_item_generator fixture to accept and set: payment_method_type, payment_method_name, cc_brand, cc_first_digits, cc_last_digits, cc_exp_month, cc_exp_year (defaulting to None) when creating a TransactionItem.
- In saleor/graphql/order/tests/queries/test_order_with_where.py, add a parametrized test test_orders_filter_by_transaction_payment_details that:
  - Generates multiple transactions across different orders with differing payment_method_type values and card brands using the fixture.
  - Executes the ORDERS_WHERE_QUERY with variables using where: { transactions: { paymentMethodDetails: ... } } in these cases:
    - Filter by type eq CARD -> expect appropriate orders.
    - Filter by type eq OTHER -> expect appropriate orders.
    - Filter by card.brand eq values (e.g., Brand, Brand4, Brand2) -> expect orders with matching brands.
    - Filter by type oneOf [CARD, OTHER] -> expect all targeted orders.
    - Filter by card.brand oneOf [Brand2, Brand4] -> expect matching orders.
  - Asserts the returned order numbers match expected indices.

6) Changelog
- In CHANGELOG.md, under unreleased order filtering bullets, add a new sub-bullet noting the ability to filter by associated payment method details (type and card brand).

Behavioral summary:
- New GraphQL filters enable narrowing orders by transactions' payment method type and, for card payments, by the card brand.
- When both a type and a card filter are provided, the card filter is applied and the type filter is ignored.
- The filters operate by correlating orders to TransactionItem rows with an EXISTS subquery for performance, backed by new BTree indexes on the relevant columns.

Implement a denormalized number_of_orders counter for users and maintain it across order lifecycle events.

Scope and observable behavior:

1) Data model
- Add a new field to saleor/account/models.py on the User model:
  - number_of_orders: Positive integer counter of orders placed by the user
  - Must default to 0 and have a database default of 0

2) Migrations
- Create a migration to add the number_of_orders field on the User model (e.g., 0090_user_number_of_orders.py).
- Create a follow-up migration to populate existing data (e.g., 0091_populate_user_number_of_orders.py) that:
  - Registers a post_migrate hook (using django.db.models.signals.post_migrate) that schedules a Celery task to populate the new counter after the order app finishes migrations.
  - Uses a Celery task (see 3) to perform the population asynchronously.

3) Backfill task for existing users
- Add a Celery task module under saleor/account/migrations/tasks/saleor3_22.py with a task function populate_user_number_of_orders_task that:
  - Iterates users in batches (e.g., BATCH_SIZE=1000) ordered by PK.
  - For the current batch of user IDs, counts non-draft orders (exclude OrderStatus.DRAFT) per user and updates each user’s number_of_orders within a single atomic transaction.
  - Uses select_for_update(of=("self",)) on User rows when updating to avoid race conditions, and bulk_update to commit changes.
  - Continues by re-scheduling itself (delay) with the last processed user PK until completion.
  - Is wrapped with allow_writer to ensure writes are allowed on the writer DB.

4) Lock helper
- Create saleor/account/lock_objects.py with a helper function user_qs_select_for_update() that returns a User queryset ordered by pk and locked using select_for_update(of=("self",)). This helper must be used in write paths that update the user counter.

5) Increment counter on order creation
- In saleor/order/actions.py, when order_created is triggered and the order has a user, increment that user’s number_of_orders by 1 using an atomic, DB-side operation (F expression) and save only the updated field.

6) Bulk order creation integration
- In saleor/graphql/order/bulk_mutations/order_bulk_create.py:
  - Accumulate per-user order counts in memory while preparing orders (only when an order is associated to a user).
  - After the transaction that creates orders completes, schedule a post-commit hook (transaction.on_commit) to call a new utility (see 7) that updates the number_of_orders field for all affected users in one batched DB update.

7) Utility to update counters for multiple users
- In saleor/account/utils.py implement update_user_orders_count(user_orders_count: dict[int, int]) that:
  - Filters to users with positive counts.
  - Executes within a traced atomic transaction.
  - Locks the target users via user_qs_select_for_update.
  - Applies atomic, DB-side increments (F("number_of_orders") + count) and bulk_update to persist the new values.

8) Decrement counter when expired orders are deleted
- In saleor/order/tasks.py, in delete_expired_orders_task:
  - Before deleting the expired orders, compute a per-user count of orders to be deleted (excluding null user_id) using the replica for reads.
  - After deletion, call a helper reduce_user_number_of_orders(user_orders_count) to decrement the number_of_orders for the impacted users.
- Implement reduce_user_number_of_orders(user_orders_count: dict[int, int]) in the same file that:
  - Runs under allow_writer and a traced atomic transaction.
  - Locks relevant users via user_qs_select_for_update, then decrements number_of_orders by the respective count, not allowing negative values (floor at 0).
  - Persists changes via bulk_update.

9) Tests and assertions
- Update checkout completion and order creation tests to reflect user association and to assert that number_of_orders increments by 1 for the associated customer:
  - saleor/graphql/checkout/tests/mutations/test_checkout_complete_with_payment.py: ensure checkout.user is set to customer_user; assert user counter increments after order completion.
  - saleor/graphql/checkout/tests/mutations/test_checkout_complete_with_transactions.py: ensure checkout.user is set; assert increment on both authorized and charged flows.
  - saleor/graphql/order/tests/mutations/test_draft_order_complete.py: set order.user and assert increment when draft order is completed.
  - saleor/graphql/order/tests/mutations/test_order_bulk_create.py: assert counter increments by the number of created orders for that user, including multiple orders case.
  - saleor/order/tests/test_order_actions.py: ensure order.user is set; assert increment after order_created event triggers.
  - saleor/order/tests/test_tasks.py: add a test that sets up expired orders for two users, runs delete_expired_orders_task, and asserts that number_of_orders decrements accordingly and does not go negative.

10) Concurrency, transactions, and DB routing
- All updates to number_of_orders must be performed inside atomic transactions, with select_for_update locks and F expressions to avoid race conditions.
- Writes must be wrapped or decorated to use allow_writer where required; reads from the batch deletion source can use the replica (consistent with existing pattern).

Non-goals / exclusions
- Do not change observable API schemas or external payloads beyond the new denormalized behavior.
- Do not include code in the spec; describe the structural and behavioral requirements only.

Implement a denormalized counter of how many orders each user has placed and keep it accurate across order creation and expiration.

Requirements:
- Add a numeric field on the user that represents their order count and backfill it for existing users.
- Increment this counter when an order is created for a user, including cases where orders are created via checkout completion or bulk order creation.
- Decrement the counter when expired orders are deleted, ensuring the counter does not drop below zero.
- Update the relevant flows to perform counter updates in a transaction-safe way (row locking + DB-side increments), and use post-commit hooks where appropriate so counters reflect only successfully created orders.
- Provide a background task to backfill the counter for existing data, processing users in batches.
- Add or adjust tests to verify that the counter increments on order creation (including draft completion and both payment/transaction flows), increments properly for bulk creation (single and multiple), and decrements after expired order deletion.

Use the project’s existing transaction tracing, writer/replica access control, and Celery setup patterns. Keep changes scoped to the user model, order actions/tasks, supporting account utilities, and tests.

+from collections import defaultdict
+
+from django.db import transaction
+
+from ....celeryconf import app
+from ....core.db.connection import allow_writer
+from ....order import OrderStatus
+from ....order.models import Order
+from ...models import User
+
+BATCH_SIZE = 1000
+
+
+@app.task
+@allow_writer()
+def populate_user_number_of_orders_task(user_pk=0):
+    users = User.objects.filter(pk__gt=user_pk).order_by("pk")
+    user_ids = list(users.values_list("id", flat=True)[:BATCH_SIZE])
+
+    if not user_ids:
+        return
+
+    user_total_orders = defaultdict(int)
+    orders = (
+        Order.objects.exclude(status=OrderStatus.DRAFT)
+        .filter(user_id__in=user_ids)
+        .values("user_id", "id")
+    )
+
+    for order in orders:
+        user_total_orders[order["user_id"]] += 1
+
+    with transaction.atomic():
+        users = (
+            User.objects.filter(pk__in=user_ids)
+            .order_by("pk")
+            .select_for_update(of=(["self"]))
+        )
+        users_to_update = []
+        for user in users:
+            total_orders = user_total_orders.get(user.id)
+
+            # Skip if the total orders count is the same to avoid unnecessary updates
+            if total_orders == user.number_of_orders:
+                continue
+
+            user.number_of_orders = total_orders
+            users_to_update.append(user)
+
+        User.objects.bulk_update(users_to_update, ["number_of_orders"])
+
+    populate_user_number_of_orders_task.delay(user_ids[-1])
